In 1973, he began planning for China’s rise in rare-earth technologies, and by the early 1990s he foresaw the geopolitical power of China’s tightening grip on rare earths, declarin g: “The Middle East has oil. China has rare earths.” 1964年，后来成为中国最高领导人的邓小平视察了位于中国北方的全球最大稀土矿。1973年，他开始规划中国在稀土技术领域的崛起。到了20世纪90年代初，他预见到了中国收紧对稀土掌控的地缘政治力量，并 宣称 ：“中东有石油，中国有稀土。” The United States and Europe are only now restarting a rare-earth industry — from the mines to the manufactured magnets — but will need at least five years and probably 10 to catch up, according to Bradsher’s book, which suggests ways to speed up the recovery. Meanwhile, Beijing has wielded its almost total control over the world’s supply of crucial rare earths to force the Trump administration and European Union to back down repeatedly on tariffs and to put heavy pressure on Japan not to support Taiwan. 美国和欧洲现在才刚刚开始重启稀土产业——从矿山开采到磁体制造——但柏凯斯在书中说，至少需要五年、甚至可能10年时间才能赶上中国，该书还提出了加速复苏的建议。与此同时，北京利用其对全球关键稀土供应几近绝对的控制权迫使特朗普政府和欧盟在关税问题上屡次让步，并向日本施加巨大压力，要求其不协助台湾。 You add it all up and China’s dominance in global manufacturing is extraordinary. Jens Eskelund, the head of the European Union Chamber of Commerce in China, citing information from members, told me that 90 percent of global manufactured goods move in containers. The percentage of global container exports by China rose from 31.8 percent in 2019 to 37.5 percent in 2025, he said. “The rolling three-month average for the most recent months is now 40 percent,” he said. The reason? China’s manufacturing output rose 5.3 percent during the first eight months of this year, he said. (Meanwhile, China’s domestic retail sales increased only 0.4 percent year on year in August, he pointed out.) 综合以上所有因素，中国在全球制造业中的主导地位是非同凡响的。中国欧盟商会主席彦辞(Jens Eskelund)引用成员提供的信息告诉我，全球90%的工业制成品是通过集装箱运输的。他说，中国在全球集装箱出口中所占的比例从2019年的31.8%上升到了2025年的37.5%。“最近几个月的每三个月滚动平均值现在已经达到了40%，”他说。原因何在？他表示，今年前八个月中国的制造业产量增长了5.3%。（同时他指出，8月份中国国内零售销售额同比仅增长了0.4%。） In 2019, China exported about 2.5 containers to Europe for every container shipped in the opposite direction, Eskelund told me. During the first eight months of 2026, the ratio widened to six containers moving from China to Europe for every one container moving from Europe to China. 彦辞告诉我，在2019年，欧洲每向中国运送一个集装箱，中国就向欧洲出口约2.5个集装箱。在2026年的前八个月，这一比例扩大到了6:1，即中国向欧洲运送六个集装箱，欧洲向中国运送一个集装箱。 “I tell the Chinese: ‘Guys, trade becomes inherently volatile if you cannot point to value creation for both sides.’” Eskelund added. “China actually understands the world’s concerns. For China, though, the question is: Why should we accommodate these concerns when the world has not put up any serious resistance?” “我告诉中国人：‘伙计们，如果你们不能证明能为双方创造价值，贸易就必然会变得动荡。’”彦辞补充道。“中国其实理解世界的担忧。但对中国来说，问题在于：既然世界并没有进行任何认真的抵抗，我们为什么要在意这些担忧呢？” It is a good question. And one that prompts me to leave this trip with some free advice to China and America from someone who believes the world will be a more prosperous and stable place if people in both countries thrive. 这是一个好问题。 这促使我在结束这次行程时，作为一个相信如果两国人民都能繁荣发展，世界将会变得更加繁荣稳定的人，向中国和美国提供一些免费的建议。 To China: You are going too far too fast too alone, and in the process you are creating too many economic relationships with too many developed and developing countries that are not win-win but win-lose. As a result of your domestic economic weakness, combined with your huge advantage in homegrown engineering talent, unparalleled manufacturing supply chains, the unrivaled work ethic of your people and your high savings rate plowed into the world’s best transportation and electricity infrastructure, China just can’t stop itself from making everything for everyone. 对中国：你走得太远、太快，也太形单影只了。在这个过程中，你与太多发达国家和发展中国家建立了太多非双赢、而是“赢-输”的经济关系。由于国内经济疲软，加上本土工程人才的巨大优势、无与伦比的制造供应链、无可匹敌的国民职业道德以及高储蓄率，被投入到全球最顶尖的交通和电力基础设施中，中国已经无法阻止自己为全世界制造一切。 I don’t know when, I don’t how, but the rest of the world will not let that happen — not when robots and A.I. are also creating steadily more worker layoffs. China is courting a real backlash. As Eskelund bluntly put it to me: “There is now a real risk we get into a trade war. We are not going to tolerate a world where China makes everything, and we just give museum tours.” 我不知道是什么时候，也不知道会以什么方式，但世界其他地区不会任由这种情况发生——尤其是在机器人和人工智能也正稳步导致更多工人失业的时候。中国正在招致真正的反弹。正如彦辞对我直言不讳地说的那样：“现在我们陷入贸易战的风险很切实。我们不会容忍一个中国包揽一切制造，而我们只能带着人去参观博物馆的世界。” To my fellow Americans (and our E.U. allies): China is not going to slow down in manufacturing as a favor to anyone. If we want to influence China’s geopolitics and geoeconomics in the age of A.I., we have to create the economic competitiveness that would compel it to do so. That requires the United States to be as serious as the people here are. 对我的美国同胞（以及我们的欧盟盟友）：中国不会放慢制造业的步伐来作为一种恩惠。如果在这个人工智能时代，我们想要影响中国的地缘政治和地缘经济，我们必须创造出迫使它做出改变的经济竞争力。这要求美国必须像这里的人们一样认真对待。 In my view, the Chinese today are getting the best out of a bad system of government — by thinking long-term and executing on a plan to align their country with the economic trends of the 21st century. 在我看来，今天的中国人正在从一个糟糕的政府体制中榨取最好的结果——通过长远思考并执行一项让他们的国家与21世纪经济趋势接轨的计划。 But one of the weaknesses of China’s system has been on dramatic display lately: the sudden disappearance and arrests of senior officials accused of corruption — so many that it could start to slow down the whole system here, if high-level bureaucrats fear making spending decisions that could land them in jail. Or as one Chinese economist put it to me, quoting a Chinese proverb: “If the water is too clear, there will be no fish.” 但中国体制的弱点之一最近戏剧性地暴露了出来：被控腐败的高级官员突然失踪和 被捕 ——人数之多，以至于如果高层官僚害怕做出可能让他们入狱的开支决策，这可能开始拖累这里的整个系统。或者正如一位中国经济学家引用一句中国谚语对我说的那样：“水至清则无鱼”。 And America? By doing no long-term thinking, appointing incompetent cabinet secretaries and having each new administration undo major initiatives of the previous one — like on clean energy — we’re getting the worst out of a good system. 而美国呢？因为缺乏长远思考，任命不称职的内阁部长，并且每一届新政府都会推翻前一届政府的重大举措（比如在清洁能源方面），我们正在把一个好体制折腾出最坏的结果。 Just look around. Republicans are spending more than $200 million to elect a terrible man — an impeached Texas attorney general, Ken Paxton — to be Texas’ next senator. Trump is savaging America’s scientific research budget and driving away the most talented foreigners who want to come to America to work, study and invent. Trump gutted the electric car industry in favor of gas guzzlers, while Democrats did not think it was a bad idea to leave our southern border porous, which helped to get Trump re-elected. 抬头看看四周吧。共和党人正斥资超过2亿美元帮助一个糟糕的人——被弹劾的得克萨斯州总检察长肯·帕克斯顿——竞选得克萨斯州参议员。特朗普正在 大肆削减 美国的科学研究预算，并赶走那些想来美国工作、学习和发明的最优秀的外籍人才。特朗普摧毁了电动汽车产业以迎合高油耗汽车，而民主党人则不认为让我们南部边境形同虚设是个坏主意，这反过来又有助于特朗普的再度当选。 The only way we will restore some balance to the economic relationship between China and America (and between China and Europe) is not by begging Beijing but by rebuilding our leverage — by being serious again about our governance, by making cost-competitive products and by planning beyond next week and then executing on those plans. 我们要在美中（以及中欧）经济关系中恢复一些平衡，唯一的方法不是去乞求北京，而是要重建我们的筹码——再次认真对待我们的国家治理，制造具有成本竞争力的产品，以及制定目光不仅限于下周的长期计划并切实去执行。 I know just what to call this strategy — I saw it on a red baseball cap the other day: “Make America Great Again.” 我完全知道该怎么称呼这个战略——前几天我在一顶红色棒球帽上看到了它：“让美国再次伟大。” If only we could start electing people who knew how. 要是我们能开始把那些知道怎么做的人选上去就好了。 托马斯·L·弗里德曼(Thomas L. Friedman)是外交事务方面的专栏作者。他1981年加入时报，曾三次获得普利策奖。他著有七本书，包括赢得国家图书奖的《从贝鲁特到耶路撒冷》(From Beirut to Jerusalem)。欢迎在 X 和 Facebook 上关注他。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 在天安门屠杀现场，我目睹了中国人民非凡的勇气
items.description: 纪思道2026年11月2日 This story is part of a series marking 175 years of eyewitness journalism from The New York Times. Read more here. 本文是《纽约时报》为纪念创刊175周年来坚守现场报道而推出的系列报道之一。阅读更多内容。 As I pedaled my bicycle toward the gunfire and Tiananmen Square, dodging people in crowds fleeing in the opposite direction, I kept thinking: What a crazy occupation this is. 当我骑着自行车朝枪声传来的方向、向天安门广场赶去时，一路躲避着迎面逃散的人群，心里不停地想：这真是个疯狂的职业。 For weeks during the spring of 1989, the question preoccupying the world had been whether the student-led Tiananmen demonstrations paralyzing China would end with a democratic revolution or with massacres. That night, June 3, the phone began ringing in the apartment in Beijing I shared with my wife and fellow New York Times correspondent, Sheryl WuDunn. We had our answer: Tens of thousands of army troops were forcing their way into central Beijing, mowing down crowds of unarmed protesters and bystanders who tried to resist. 1989年春天的那几周，全世界都在关注一个问题：由学生领导、使中国陷入瘫痪的天安门示威究竟会以一场民主革命告终，还是以大屠杀收场？6月3日那天夜里，我和妻子、同为《纽约时报》记者的伍洁芳(Sheryl WuDunn)在北京的公寓里，电话开始响个不停。我们得到了答案：数万名军人正强行向北京市中心推进，向试图阻挡他们的手无寸铁的抗议者和旁观者开枪射击。 So I jumped on my bicycle, legs pumping madly, careening around tank traps students had set up, so I could report on a modern army waging war on its people. 于是我跳上自行车，双腿拼命蹬着，绕过学生们设置的坦克障碍，赶去报道一支现代化军队如何向本国人民开战。 1989年5月4日，天安门广场上的抗议者。 It was probably the most important story I’ve covered and I got at least one big thing wrong — I’ll get to that — but I did manage to reach Tiananmen Square before the troops. I parked my bicycle near the famous portrait of Chairman Mao and began interviewing people in the throng of students and workers. 这也许是我记者生涯中报道过的最重要的新闻，而我至少犯了一个重大错误——这一点我稍后会谈到。不过，我确实赶在军队抵达之前进入了天安门广场。我把自行车停在那幅著名的毛主席画像附近，开始采访聚集在广场上的学生和工人。 Although it was already dark, the square was lit by overhead lights and by the glow of two armored personnel carriers that protesters had set ablaze. At first, the troops, arriving by the truckload, fired over our heads. Then they lowered their aim and fired right at us. 虽然天已经黑了，广场仍被高处的灯光和两辆被抗议者点燃的装甲运兵车发出的火光照亮。起初，乘坐一辆辆卡车抵达的军人朝我们头顶上方开枪。随后，他们压低枪口，直接向我们射击。 The gunfire was episodic, coming in cacophonous bursts every few minutes. People would fall, we would retreat, the guns would fall silent for a time and our retreat would halt. 枪声时断时续，每隔几分钟便是一阵刺耳的密集枪声。有人倒下，我们后撤，枪声沉寂下来，我们也停下后撤的脚步。 I was rushing around, interviewing people in Chinese, always trying to keep a layer of protesters between me and the bullets. Until I realized that I was taller than almost everyone around me, so that a valuable few upper inches of me were still exposed. I began stooping as I spoke to people. 我四处奔走，用中文采访，同时尽量借助人群掩护自己，躲避子弹。直到后来我才意识到，自己比周围几乎所有人都高，这意味着，我仍有要命的一小截身体暴露在枪口之下。于是，我开始弯着腰与人交谈。 “General strike!” the crowd shouted. “General strike!” Some people hurled rocks or Molotov cocktails toward the troops, but they couldn’t hit the soldiers — and then there would be another round of gunfire, and more would drop. “大罢工！大罢工！”人群高喊着。有人朝军队投掷石块或燃烧瓶，但打不到他们。紧接着又是一轮枪响，更多人应声倒下。 Groups of protesters commandeered two buses in hopes of reaching the troops. About a dozen young people boarded each bus, holding iron bars or other weapons with which they intended to attack the soldiers. The crowd screamed encouragement, but their courage was misplaced. As the protesters drove the buses toward the troops, the soldiers opened fire. The buses came to a halt, one of them on fire, and in a moment, these young people transformed from heroes into corpses. 有几群抗议者强占了两辆公共汽车，希望借此冲到军队跟前。每辆车上约有十几个年轻人，手里拿着铁棍或其他武器，打算攻击士兵。人群高声为他们鼓劲，但这份勇气用错了地方。当抗议者驾着公交车驶向军队时，士兵开火了。两辆车停了下来，其中一辆起了火，转眼之间，这些年轻人就从英雄变成了尸体。 I found myself in the midst of a massacre. With each round of gunfire, we were pushed backward on the blood-soaked Avenue of Eternal Peace. My bicycle was now close to the troops and not recoverable, so I ran to a nearby hospital to count corpses, and then back home. I had forgotten that it was a Saturday evening, which for the paper meant early deadlines. 我发现自己身处一场屠杀之中。每一轮枪声响起，都迫使我们沿着血迹斑斑的长安街向后退。我的自行车此时已离军队太近，无法取回，于是我跑到附近一家医院清点尸体，随后又赶回家中。我忘了那天是星期六晚上，而对报社来说，这意味着截稿时间要提前。 When I didn’t return on time, Sheryl, who had filed her own story about the slaughter, was increasingly fearful that I had been shot. “There’s no point in worrying,” the foreign editor, Joseph Lelyveld, kept telling her on the phone; the anxiety in his voice made her worry even more. He tried to distract her by asking her to reach out to all the hospitals to document the death toll — a request that didn’t help Sheryl’s mood. 我迟迟没有回来，已经发出自己那篇屠杀报道的伍洁芳越来越担心我中了枪。“担心也没用，”国际新闻编辑约瑟夫·莱利维尔德在电话里不断对她说，可他声音里的焦虑反而让她更加担忧。他想分散她的注意力，请她联系所有医院，统计死亡人数，这个要求丝毫没有缓解她的不安。 The New York Times Finally, I burst in, hugged Sheryl, called New York to reassure editors there that I was fine and then filed my story by telex — a few paragraphs at a time, as I wrote them. I had never been so sad to have my byline and Sheryl’s under a banner headline across the front page. 后来我终于冲进家门，拥抱伍洁芳，给纽约打电话，向编辑们报平安，然后用电传发出了我的稿子，写一段，发一段。看到我和伍洁芳的名字并列署在头版通栏大标题下，我从未像那一刻那样悲伤。 Guilt nagged at me that night, and this brings me to my first great mistake in covering the crisis. During the demonstrations in the weeks before the bloodshed, I had periodically written condescendingly that the workers and peasants in the protest movement talked about democracy but couldn’t define it. I had suggested that they were driven by anger at inflation and corruption but didn’t necessarily believe in democracy for Tibetans or fully embrace the kind of free and pluralistic society they spoke of so glowingly. 那天夜里，愧疚一直折磨着我。这就涉及我报道这场危机时犯下的第一个重大错误。在流血事件发生前的几个星期里，在报道示威活动时，我不时以居高临下的口吻写道，参加抗议的工人和农民虽然谈论民主，却说不清民主究竟是什么。我曾暗示，他们参加抗议是出于对通货膨胀和腐败的不满，却未必相信藏人也应享有民主权利，也未必完全认同他们热情赞颂的那种自由、多元的社会。 1989年6月4日，人们骑着三轮车运送天安门广场枪击事件中的受伤者。 There was something to this idea, but that night in June I had seen extraordinary courage from the workers and peasants. I was terrified that evening — my notebook was so damp with sweat from fear that I had trouble writing in it — and the bravest people of all were the poorly educated laborers from the countryside who drove bicycle rickshaws. Whenever there was a pause in the shooting, they would pedal their carts into the fray to pick up the bodies of students who had been killed or injured, then turn around and race to the hospitals. They might not have been able to define democracy but they were ready to die for it. 这种看法并非毫无道理。但6月的那个夜晚，我亲眼目睹了工人和农民非凡的勇气。那天晚上我害怕极了，笔记本被我因恐惧而流出的汗水浸得湿透，几乎在上面写不了字。而所有人中最勇敢的是那些来自农村、受教育程度不高、靠蹬三轮车谋生的劳动者。每当枪声稍歇，他们便蹬着三轮车冲进交火地带，把中弹身亡或受伤的学生抬上车，再掉头飞奔医院。他们或许说不清民主的定义，却愿意为民主献出生命。 Another hard lesson I learned covering Tiananmen: Victims lie or, more charitably, misremember. It’s human nature to doubt oppressors and believe victims, but in the aftermath of the massacre there were many “eyewitness” accounts claiming that thousands or tens of thousands of students had been slaughtered in Tiananmen Square; that huge numbers of them had been shot from machine gun emplacements there; or that many were killed when tanks rolled over tents with students inside. None of this was true. 报道天安门事件时，我还学到了另一个沉痛的教训：受害者也会说谎。或者更宽容地说，他们也会记错事实。怀疑压迫者、相信受害者，这是人之常情，但在屠杀发生后，有许多“目击者”声称，有数千甚至数万名学生在天安门广场遭到屠杀，其中大量学生被广场上架设的机枪射杀，还有许多学生在坦克碾过他们栖身的帐篷时丧生。这些说法都不属实。 Since then, I’ve seen many times in my career that perpetrators of atrocities lie to cover up their abuses, and that victims respond with exaggerations of their own. This has taught me that we must be as vigilant in verifying accounts of victims as we are in grilling oppressors. While many estimates of the Tiananmen death toll are in the thousands, I’m reasonably sure these are wrong. Sheryl and I made great efforts to cultivate sources at hospitals and morgues to determine the toll, and our best guess is that between 400 and 800 people were killed and several thousand injured. 此后，在我的记者生涯中，我多次看到暴行的实施者为了掩盖罪行而撒谎，受害者则以自己的夸大之词作出回应。这让我明白，我们核实受害者证词时，必须像质询压迫者一样保持警惕。虽然有许多估计认为天安门事件造成数千人死亡，但我相当确信，这些数字是错误的。我和伍洁芳曾竭尽全力在医院和停尸房发展信源，以确定死亡人数。我们最合理的估计是，死亡人数在400至800人之间，另有数千人受伤。 Accessing hospitals was difficult. Soldiers turned us away at entrances and doctors were threatened if they spoke to journalists. Chinese citizens and even some officials cooperated nonetheless, because they wanted the truth to come out. Disenchanted employees at one hospital sneaked us inside through a tunnel system from a neighboring building. We found that even the hallways were filled with shooting victims. 进入医院并不容易。士兵在入口处阻拦我们，医生如果与记者交谈也会受到威胁。尽管如此，仍有中国公民愿意配合，甚至一些官员也是如此，因为他们希望真相能够公之于众。一家医院里，有几名心灰意冷的员工悄悄带我们从邻近建筑的地下通道进入医院。我们发现，就连走廊里也躺满了枪伤患者。 1989年4月下旬，纪思道在一场学生抗议游行中。 One young wife was weeping beside the unconscious figure of her husband, an inventor with seven patents in his name. Despite her warnings, he had gone out when the shooting started, in order to support the students, and she loved and admired him for his courage. But, she added between sobs, she hated that he might leave her alone with their 4-year-old daughter. 一位年轻妻子在昏迷不醒的丈夫身旁哭泣。她的丈夫是一名发明家，名下拥有七项专利。枪击开始后，尽管妻子曾劝阻，他还是出门声援学生。她爱他，也钦佩他的勇气。但她抽泣着补充说，她恨他可能就这样丢下自己和他们四岁的女儿。 Journalists like to project toughness, but I was shattered, physically and morally exhausted. We went days with barely a wink of sleep, and once, when we did nap, the army fired on our apartment compound with automatic weapons. Moving around Beijing to interview people, Sheryl and I were afraid of being shot, but worse was to see the hopeful, vibrant China we had been covering morph into a crushing dictatorship. I remember collapsing on my bed one day and finding tears trickling down my cheeks. 记者总喜欢表现得坚强，但我当时已经彻底崩溃，身心俱疲。我们连续几天几乎没有合眼。有一次，我们好不容易小睡片刻，军队却用自动武器向我们居住的公寓区开火。我和伍洁芳在北京四处采访时，一直担心自己会中枪。但更令人痛苦的是，看着我们一直报道的那个充满希望、生机勃勃的中国正在变成一个令人窒息的独裁国家。我记得有一天，我瘫倒在床上，眼泪顺着脸颊流下来。 The Chinese government rewrote history, calling the protesters “hoodlums” who had engaged in “rioting.” The state media singled me out, denouncing me for spreading lies and “writing not news reports but fiction.” The next day I ordered lunch at an empty Sichuan restaurant, where the staff gathered in a corner, pointing to me and whispering. I feared they had recognized me and I wondered if they might poison my food. Then several waitresses approached my table. “Are you the one they mentioned on television last night?” one asked. “The reporter who lies?” 中国政府改写了历史，将抗议者称为参与“暴乱”的“暴徒”。官方媒体专门点名谴责我，说我散布谎言，“写的不是新闻报道，而是小说”。第二天，我在一家空荡荡的川菜馆点了午饭，服务员们聚在角落里，指着我窃窃私语。我担心他们认出了我，不禁怀疑他们会不会在饭菜里下毒。随后，几名女服务员走到我的餐桌前。“你就是昨天晚上电视里说的那个人吗？”其中一人问，“那个撒谎的记者？” 1989年6月6日，天安门广场大屠杀发生两天后，北京街头的军用坦克。 “Yes,” I said, and I started to explain, but she cut me off. “Never mind,” she said, beaming. “There’s no need to pay your bill. We’ll take care of it. We’re all ‘hoodlums’ here.” “是的，”我回答，正要解释，她却打断了我。“没关系，”她笑容满面地说，“不用付账了，我们请客。我们这里都是‘暴徒’。” As the government began mass arrests, one of our sources was a Chinese student whom we had inadvertently gotten into trouble. “Shawn,” as he called himself in English, was a student at Tsinghua University who had helped us cover the protests. Now he was being interrogated about his connection to us, yet he still dared to meet secretly with Sheryl — who is Chinese American and could melt into crowds in a way I could not — to update her on the crackdown at the universities. His courage was breathtaking, and we were frightened for him when he suddenly disappeared. 政府开始大规模逮捕，而我们的一名消息来源——一位中国学生——因我们的无心之失而陷入了麻烦。他给自己取了个英文名字叫“Shawn”（肖恩），是清华大学的学生，曾帮助我们报道抗议活动。如今，他正因为与我们的关系而受到审问。尽管如此，他仍敢冒险与伍洁芳秘密见面，向她通报当局在大学校园里的镇压行动——伍洁芳是华裔美国人，能够像普通中国人一样融入人群，而我做不到。肖恩的勇气令人惊叹。当他突然失踪时，我们非常担心他的安危。 This incident brings me to another moment that I still turn over in my mind. More than a year after his disappearance, Shawn reappeared in Beijing, met with me in secret and explained what had happened: He had been imprisoned but had escaped and was on the run. Now he asked for my help in fleeing China. 这件事让我想起另一个至今仍在脑海中反复思量的时刻。失踪一年多后，肖恩重新出现在北京，秘密与我见面，讲述了他的遭遇：他曾被监禁，但后来越狱逃了出来，如今正在逃亡。他请求我帮助他逃离中国。 One basic rule of being a foreign correspondent is that you obey local laws. You certainly don’t help an escaped felon leave the country. Yet here was a young man who had endured prison because he had helped us cover this story. If we didn’t assist him, he would almost certainly be caught. 作为外派记者，有一条基本准则就是遵守所在国法律。无论如何，你都不应该帮助一名越狱的重罪犯逃离该国。然而，站在我面前的这个年轻人，正是因为帮助我们报道这件事才遭受牢狱之灾。如果我们不帮他，他几乎肯定会再次被捕。 What to do? I wanted to consult editors in New York, but that was impossible because my phones were tapped. In any case, no editor could recommend helping an escaped prisoner. 该怎么办？我想征询纽约编辑的意见，但这不可能，因为我的电话受到监听。无论如何，也不会有哪个编辑建议帮助一名越狱囚犯。 Another concern: I harbored a nagging doubt about Shawn’s story. He said he had escaped while working in the fields of a prison farm, but we had never heard of anyone escaping from a Chinese prison. I wondered, Could this be a setup? The Chinese prime minister at the time, Li Peng, disliked my coverage, and his office was looking for an excuse to expel me. Was Chinese state security hoping to entrap me so that the authorities could arrest and imprison me and close The Times’s bureau? 我还有另一个顾虑：我始终对肖恩的说法存有一丝疑虑。他说自己是在监狱农场干农活时逃出来的，但我们从未听说过有人能从中国的监狱越狱。我不禁怀疑：这会不会是个圈套？当时的中国总理李鹏不喜欢我的报道，他的办公室正在寻找借口将我驱逐出境。中国国家安全机关是不是想诱我上钩，好让当局逮捕并监禁我，同时关闭《纽约时报》北京分社？ I wavered, but Sheryl had a firmer compass. She doubted that Shawn would agree to entrap me, and she insisted that, given the risks he had taken, we owed him our assistance. So we did help him, including providing money to finance his escape. 我犹豫不决，但伍洁芳的判断更加坚定。她不相信肖恩会同意设局陷害我，而且她坚持认为，鉴于他曾冒过那么大的风险，我们有义务帮助他。于是，我们确实出手相助，包括出钱资助他逃亡。 Shawn was able to slip into Hong Kong on Christmas Day, 1990, when he figured there would be fewer British police officers along the border. He called me that night, and the next day I flew to Hong Kong, where, with the help of Human Rights Watch, I negotiated to get him a visa to the United States. Shawn is now a U.S. citizen. 1990年圣诞节那天，肖恩成功潜入香港。他认为那天边境一带的英国警察可能会少一些。当天晚上，他给我打了电话。第二天，我飞往香港，在人权观察组织的协助下，通过交涉为他争取到了美国签证。如今，肖恩已成为美国公民。 Once I was out of China and could speak freely on the phone, I confessed to the paper’s top editors what I had done. To my surprise, they were congratulatory rather than scolding. A retired executive editor, A.M. Rosenthal, confided that three decades earlier he had helped sneak someone from Communist Poland to the West. And a Times correspondent, Sydney Schanberg, had tried desperately (though unsuccessfully) to doctor a fake passport for a Cambodian colleague, Dith Pran, to save him from the Khmer Rouge slaughter. Dith Pran eventually made it out on his own and worked as a much-loved colleague in The Times’s newsroom, a constant reminder that we have complex human obligations as well as professional ones. 等我离开中国、能在电话里自由交谈时，我就向报社高层编辑坦白了自己的所作所为。出乎意料的是，他们非但没有责备我，反而向我表示祝贺。已经退休的执行总编辑A·M·罗森塔尔私下告诉我，30年前，他曾帮助一名身在共产主义波兰的人秘密逃往西方。《纽约时报》记者悉尼·尚伯格也曾竭尽全力，试图为柬埔寨同事迪斯·普兰伪造护照，帮助他逃过红色高棉的屠杀，虽然最终没有成功。迪斯·普兰后来凭自己的努力逃了出来，在《纽约时报》的新闻编辑部成为了一位深受爱戴的同事。这时刻提醒着我们：除了职业责任，我们还肩负着复杂的人道义务。 There’s nothing I’ve done in my career that was as unprofessional as helping Shawn. But there are also few things I’m prouder of. 在我的整个职业生涯中，没有哪件事比帮助肖恩更不符合职业规范。但也很少有哪件事能让我如此自豪。 纪思道(Nicholas Kristof) 2001起成为时报专栏作家，曾两次获得普利策奖。他最新出版的回忆录名为《追逐希望：一名记者的报道生涯》(“Chasing Hope: A Reporter’s Life”)。欢迎在X上关注他：@NickKristof。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
items.content: 纪思道 2026年11月2日 This story is part of a series marking 175 years of eyewitness journalism from The New York Times. Read more here. 本文是《纽约时报》为纪念创刊175周年来坚守现场报道而推出的系列报道之一 。 阅读更多内容。 As I pedaled my bicycle toward the gunfire and Tiananmen Square, dodging people in crowds fleeing in the opposite direction, I kept thinking: What a crazy occupation this is. 当我骑着自行车朝枪声传来的方向、向天安门广场赶去时，一路躲避着迎面逃散的人群，心里不停地想：这真是个疯狂的职业。 For weeks during the spring of 1989, the question preoccupying the world had been whether the student-led Tiananmen demonstrations paralyzing China would end with a democratic revolution or with massacres. That night, June 3, the phone began ringing in the apartment in Beijing I shared with my wife and fellow New York Times correspondent, Sheryl WuDunn. We had our answer: Tens of thousands of army troops were forcing their way into central Beijing, mowing down crowds of unarmed protesters and bystanders who tried to resist. 1989年春天的那几周，全世界都在关注一个问题：由学生领导、使中国陷入瘫痪的天安门示威究竟会以一场民主革命告终，还是以大屠杀收场？6月3日那天夜里，我和妻子、同为《纽约时报》记者的伍洁芳(Sheryl WuDunn)在北京的公寓里，电话开始响个不停。我们得到了答案：数万名军人正强行向北京市中心推进，向试图阻挡他们的手无寸铁的抗议者和旁观者开枪射击。 So I jumped on my bicycle, legs pumping madly, careening around tank traps students had set up, so I could report on a modern army waging war on its people. 于是我跳上自行车，双腿拼命蹬着，绕过学生们设置的坦克障碍，赶去报道一支现代化军队如何向本国人民开战。 1989年5月4日，天安门广场上的抗议者。 It was probably the most important story I’ve covered and I got at least one big thing wrong — I’ll get to that — but I did manage to reach Tiananmen Square before the troops. I parked my bicycle near the famous portrait of Chairman Mao and began interviewing people in the throng of students and workers. 这也许是我记者生涯中报道过的最重要的新闻，而我至少犯了一个重大错误——这一点我稍后会谈到。不过，我确实赶在军队抵达之前进入了天安门广场。我把自行车停在那幅著名的毛主席画像附近，开始采访聚集在广场上的学生和工人。 Although it was already dark, the square was lit by overhead lights and by the glow of two armored personnel carriers that protesters had set ablaze. At first, the troops, arriving by the truckload, fired over our heads. Then they lowered their aim and fired right at us. 虽然天已经黑了，广场仍被高处的灯光和两辆被抗议者点燃的装甲运兵车发出的火光照亮。起初，乘坐一辆辆卡车抵达的军人朝我们头顶上方开枪。随后，他们压低枪口，直接向我们射击。 The gunfire was episodic, coming in cacophonous bursts every few minutes. People would fall, we would retreat, the guns would fall silent for a time and our retreat would halt. 枪声时断时续，每隔几分钟便是一阵刺耳的密集枪声。有人倒下，我们后撤，枪声沉寂下来，我们也停下后撤的脚步。 I was rushing around, interviewing people in Chinese, always trying to keep a layer of protesters between me and the bullets. Until I realized that I was taller than almost everyone around me, so that a valuable few upper inches of me were still exposed. I began stooping as I spoke to people. 我四处奔走，用中文采访，同时尽量借助人群掩护自己，躲避子弹。直到后来我才意识到，自己比周围几乎所有人都高，这意味着，我仍有要命的一小截身体暴露在枪口之下。于是，我开始弯着腰与人交谈。 “General strike!” the crowd shouted. “General strike!” Some people hurled rocks or Molotov cocktails toward the troops, but they couldn’t hit the soldiers — and then there would be another round of gunfire, and more would drop. “大罢工！大罢工！”人群高喊着。有人朝军队投掷石块或燃烧瓶，但打不到他们。紧接着又是一轮枪响，更多人应声倒下。 Groups of protesters commandeered two buses in hopes of reaching the troops. About a dozen young people boarded each bus, holding iron bars or other weapons with which they intended to attack the soldiers. The crowd screamed encouragement, but their courage was misplaced. As the protesters drove the buses toward the troops, the soldiers opened fire. The buses came to a halt, one of them on fire, and in a moment, these young people transformed from heroes into corpses. 有几群抗议者强占了两辆公共汽车，希望借此冲到军队跟前。每辆车上约有十几个年轻人，手里拿着铁棍或其他武器，打算攻击士兵。人群高声为他们鼓劲，但这份勇气用错了地方。当抗议者驾着公交车驶向军队时，士兵开火了。两辆车停了下来，其中一辆起了火，转眼之间，这些年轻人就从英雄变成了尸体。 I found myself in the midst of a massacre. With each round of gunfire, we were pushed backward on the blood-soaked Avenue of Eternal Peace. My bicycle was now close to the troops and not recoverable, so I ran to a nearby hospital to count corpses, and then back home. I had forgotten that it was a Saturday evening, which for the paper meant early deadlines. 我发现自己身处一场屠杀之中。每一轮枪声响起，都迫使我们沿着血迹斑斑的长安街向后退。我的自行车此时已离军队太近，无法取回，于是我跑到附近一家医院清点尸体，随后又赶回家中。我忘了那天是星期六晚上，而对报社来说，这意味着截稿时间要提前。 When I didn’t return on time, Sheryl, who had filed her own story about the slaughter, was increasingly fearful that I had been shot. “There’s no point in worrying,” the foreign editor, Joseph Lelyveld, kept telling her on the phone; the anxiety in his voice made her worry even more. He tried to distract her by asking her to reach out to all the hospitals to document the death toll — a request that didn’t help Sheryl’s mood. 我迟迟没有回来，已经发出自己那篇屠杀报道的伍洁芳越来越担心我中了枪。“担心也没用，”国际新闻编辑约瑟夫·莱利维尔德在电话里不断对她说，可他声音里的焦虑反而让她更加担忧。他想分散她的注意力，请她联系所有医院，统计死亡人数，这个要求丝毫没有缓解她的不安。 The New York Times Finally, I burst in, hugged Sheryl, called New York to reassure editors there that I was fine and then filed my story by telex — a few paragraphs at a time, as I wrote them. I had never been so sad to have my byline and Sheryl’s under a banner headline across the front page. 后来我终于冲进家门，拥抱伍洁芳，给纽约打电话，向编辑们报平安，然后用电传发出了我的稿子，写一段，发一段。看到我和伍洁芳的名字并列署在头版通栏大标题下，我从未像那一刻那样悲伤。 Guilt nagged at me that night, and this brings me to my first great mistake in covering the crisis. During the demonstrations in the weeks before the bloodshed, I had periodically written condescendingly that the workers and peasants in the protest movement talked about democracy but couldn’t define it. I had suggested that they were driven by anger at inflation and corruption but didn’t necessarily believe in democracy for Tibetans or fully embrace the kind of free and pluralistic society they spoke of so glowingly. 那天夜里，愧疚一直折磨着我。这就涉及我报道这场危机时犯下的第一个重大错误。在流血事件发生前的几个星期里，在报道示威活动时，我不时以居高临下的口吻写道，参加抗议的工人和农民虽然谈论民主，却说不清民主究竟是什么。我曾暗示，他们参加抗议是出于对通货膨胀和腐败的不满，却未必相信藏人也应享有民主权利，也未必完全认同他们热情赞颂的那种自由、多元的社会。 1989年6月4日，人们骑着三轮车运送天安门广场枪击事件中的受伤者。 There was something to this idea, but that night in June I had seen extraordinary courage from the workers and peasants. I was terrified that evening — my notebook was so damp with sweat from fear that I had trouble writing in it — and the bravest people of all were the poorly educated laborers from the countryside who drove bicycle rickshaws. Whenever there was a pause in the shooting, they would pedal their carts into the fray to pick up the bodies of students who had been killed or injured, then turn around and race to the hospitals. They might not have been able to define democracy but they were ready to die for it. 这种看法并非毫无道理。但6月的那个夜晚，我亲眼目睹了工人和农民非凡的勇气。那天晚上我害怕极了，笔记本被我因恐惧而流出的汗水浸得湿透，几乎在上面写不了字。而所有人中最勇敢的是那些来自农村、受教育程度不高、靠蹬三轮车谋生的劳动者。每当枪声稍歇，他们便蹬着三轮车冲进交火地带，把中弹身亡或受伤的学生抬上车，再掉头飞奔医院。他们或许说不清民主的定义，却愿意为民主献出生命。 Another hard lesson I learned covering Tiananmen: Victims lie or, more charitably, misremember. It’s human nature to doubt oppressors and believe victims, but in the aftermath of the massacre there were many “eyewitness” accounts claiming that thousands or tens of thousands of students had been slaughtered in Tiananmen Square; that huge numbers of them had been shot from machine gun emplacements there; or that many were killed when tanks rolled over tents with students inside. None of this was true. 报道天安门事件时，我还学到了另一个沉痛的教训：受害者也会说谎。或者更宽容地说，他们也会记错事实。怀疑压迫者、相信受害者，这是人之常情，但在屠杀发生后，有许多“目击者”声称，有数千甚至数万名学生在天安门广场遭到屠杀，其中大量学生被广场上架设的机枪射杀，还有许多学生在坦克碾过他们栖身的帐篷时丧生。这些说法都不属实。 Since then, I’ve seen many times in my career that perpetrators of atrocities lie to cover up their abuses, and that victims respond with exaggerations of their own. This has taught me that we must be as vigilant in verifying accounts of victims as we are in grilling oppressors. While many estimates of the Tiananmen death toll are in the thousands, I’m reasonably sure these are wrong. Sheryl and I made great efforts to cultivate sources at hospitals and morgues to determine the toll, and our best guess is that between 400 and 800 people were killed and several thousand injured. 此后，在我的记者生涯中，我多次看到暴行的实施者为了掩盖罪行而撒谎，受害者则以自己的夸大之词作出回应。这让我明白，我们核实受害者证词时，必须像质询压迫者一样保持警惕。虽然有许多估计认为天安门事件造成数千人死亡，但我相当确信，这些数字是错误的。我和伍洁芳曾竭尽全力在医院和停尸房发展信源，以确定死亡人数。我们最合理的估计是，死亡人数在400至800人之间，另有数千人受伤。 Accessing hospitals was difficult. Soldiers turned us away at entrances and doctors were threatened if they spoke to journalists. Chinese citizens and even some officials cooperated nonetheless, because they wanted the truth to come out. Disenchanted employees at one hospital sneaked us inside through a tunnel system from a neighboring building. We found that even the hallways were filled with shooting victims. 进入医院并不容易。士兵在入口处阻拦我们，医生如果与记者交谈也会受到威胁。尽管如此，仍有中国公民愿意配合，甚至一些官员也是如此，因为他们希望真相能够公之于众。一家医院里，有几名心灰意冷的员工悄悄带我们从邻近建筑的地下通道进入医院。我们发现，就连走廊里也躺满了枪伤患者。 1989年4月下旬，纪思道在一场学生抗议游行中。 One young wife was weeping beside the unconscious figure of her husband, an inventor with seven patents in his name. Despite her warnings, he had gone out when the shooting started, in order to support the students, and she loved and admired him for his courage. But, she added between sobs, she hated that he might leave her alone with their 4-year-old daughter. 一位年轻妻子在昏迷不醒的丈夫身旁哭泣。她的丈夫是一名发明家，名下拥有七项专利。枪击开始后，尽管妻子曾劝阻，他还是出门声援学生。她爱他，也钦佩他的勇气。但她抽泣着补充说，她恨他可能就这样丢下自己和他们四岁的女儿。 Journalists like to project toughness, but I was shattered, physically and morally exhausted. We went days with barely a wink of sleep, and once, when we did nap, the army fired on our apartment compound with automatic weapons. Moving around Beijing to interview people, Sheryl and I were afraid of being shot, but worse was to see the hopeful, vibrant China we had been covering morph into a crushing dictatorship. I remember collapsing on my bed one day and finding tears trickling down my cheeks. 记者总喜欢表现得坚强，但我当时已经彻底崩溃，身心俱疲。我们连续几天几乎没有合眼。有一次，我们好不容易小睡片刻，军队却用自动武器向我们居住的公寓区开火。我和伍洁芳在北京四处采访时，一直担心自己会中枪。但更令人痛苦的是，看着我们一直报道的那个充满希望、生机勃勃的中国正在变成一个令人窒息的独裁国家。我记得有一天，我瘫倒在床上，眼泪顺着脸颊流下来。 The Chinese government rewrote history, calling the protesters “hoodlums” who had engaged in “rioting.” The state media singled me out, denouncing me for spreading lies and “writing not news reports but fiction.” The next day I ordered lunch at an empty Sichuan restaurant, where the staff gathered in a corner, pointing to me and whispering. I feared they had recognized me and I wondered if they might poison my food. Then several waitresses approached my table. “Are you the one they mentioned on television last night?” one asked. “The reporter who lies?” 中国政府改写了历史，将抗议者称为参与“暴乱”的“暴徒”。官方媒体专门点名谴责我，说我散布谎言，“写的不是新闻报道，而是小说”。第二天，我在一家空荡荡的川菜馆点了午饭，服务员们聚在角落里，指着我窃窃私语。我担心他们认出了我，不禁怀疑他们会不会在饭菜里下毒。随后，几名女服务员走到我的餐桌前。“你就是昨天晚上电视里说的那个人吗？”其中一人问，“那个撒谎的记者？” 1989年6月6日，天安门广场大屠杀发生两天后，北京街头的军用坦克。 “Yes,” I said, and I started to explain, but she cut me off. “Never mind,” she said, beaming. “There’s no need to pay your bill. We’ll take care of it. We’re all ‘hoodlums’ here.” “是的，”我回答，正要解释，她却打断了我。“没关系，”她笑容满面地说，“不用付账了，我们请客。我们这里都是‘暴徒’。” As the government began mass arrests, one of our sources was a Chinese student whom we had inadvertently gotten into trouble. “Shawn,” as he called himself in English, was a student at Tsinghua University who had helped us cover the protests. Now he was being interrogated about his connection to us, yet he still dared to meet secretly with Sheryl — who is Chinese American and could melt into crowds in a way I could not — to update her on the crackdown at the universities. His courage was breathtaking, and we were frightened for him when he suddenly disappeared. 政府开始大规模逮捕，而我们的一名消息来源——一位中国学生——因我们的无心之失而陷入了麻烦。他给自己取了个英文名字叫“Shawn”（肖恩），是清华大学的学生，曾帮助我们报道抗议活动。如今，他正因为与我们的关系而受到审问。尽管如此，他仍敢冒险与伍洁芳秘密见面，向她通报当局在大学校园里的镇压行动——伍洁芳是华裔美国人，能够像普通中国人一样融入人群，而我做不到。肖恩的勇气令人惊叹。当他突然失踪时，我们非常担心他的安危。 This incident brings me to another moment that I still turn over in my mind. More than a year after his disappearance, Shawn reappeared in Beijing, met with me in secret and explained what had happened: He had been imprisoned but had escaped and was on the run. Now he asked for my help in fleeing China. 这件事让我想起另一个至今仍在脑海中反复思量的时刻。失踪一年多后，肖恩重新出现在北京，秘密与我见面，讲述了他的遭遇：他曾被监禁，但后来越狱逃了出来，如今正在逃亡。他请求我帮助他逃离中国。 One basic rule of being a foreign correspondent is that you obey local laws. You certainly don’t help an escaped felon leave the country. Yet here was a young man who had endured prison because he had helped us cover this story. If we didn’t assist him, he would almost certainly be caught. 作为外派记者，有一条基本准则就是遵守所在国法律。无论如何，你都不应该帮助一名越狱的重罪犯逃离该国。然而，站在我面前的这个年轻人，正是因为帮助我们报道这件事才遭受牢狱之灾。如果我们不帮他，他几乎肯定会再次被捕。 What to do? I wanted to consult editors in New York, but that was impossible because my phones were tapped. In any case, no editor could recommend helping an escaped prisoner. 该怎么办？我想征询纽约编辑的意见，但这不可能，因为我的电话受到监听。无论如何，也不会有哪个编辑建议帮助一名越狱囚犯。 Another concern: I harbored a nagging doubt about Shawn’s story. He said he had escaped while working in the fields of a prison farm, but we had never heard of anyone escaping from a Chinese prison. I wondered, Could this be a setup? The Chinese prime minister at the time, Li Peng, disliked my coverage, and his office was looking for an excuse to expel me. Was Chinese state security hoping to entrap me so that the authorities could arrest and imprison me and close The Times’s bureau? 我还有另一个顾虑：我始终对肖恩的说法存有一丝疑虑。他说自己是在监狱农场干农活时逃出来的，但我们从未听说过有人能从中国的监狱越狱。我不禁怀疑：这会不会是个圈套？当时的中国总理李鹏不喜欢我的报道，他的办公室正在寻找借口将我驱逐出境。中国国家安全机关是不是想诱我上钩，好让当局逮捕并监禁我，同时关闭《纽约时报》北京分社？ I wavered, but Sheryl had a firmer compass. She doubted that Shawn would agree to entrap me, and she insisted that, given the risks he had taken, we owed him our assistance. So we did help him, including providing money to finance his escape. 我犹豫不决，但伍洁芳的判断更加坚定。她不相信肖恩会同意设局陷害我，而且她坚持认为，鉴于他曾冒过那么大的风险，我们有义务帮助他。于是，我们确实出手相助，包括出钱资助他逃亡。 Shawn was able to slip into Hong Kong on Christmas Day, 1990, when he figured there would be fewer British police officers along the border. He called me that night, and the next day I flew to Hong Kong, where, with the help of Human Rights Watch, I negotiated to get him a visa to the United States. Shawn is now a U.S. citizen. 1990年圣诞节那天，肖恩成功潜入香港。他认为那天边境一带的英国警察可能会少一些。当天晚上，他给我打了电话。第二天，我飞往香港，在人权观察组织的协助下，通过交涉为他争取到了美国签证。如今，肖恩已成为美国公民。 Once I was out of China and could speak freely on the phone, I confessed to the paper’s top editors what I had done. To my surprise, they were congratulatory rather than scolding. A retired executive editor, A.M. Rosenthal, confided that three decades earlier he had helped sneak someone from Communist Poland to the West. And a Times correspondent, Sydney Schanberg, had tried desperately (though unsuccessfully) to doctor a fake passport for a Cambodian colleague, Dith Pran, to save him from the Khmer Rouge slaughter. Dith Pran eventually made it out on his own and worked as a much-loved colleague in The Times’s newsroom, a constant reminder that we have complex human obligations as well as professional ones. 等我离开中国、能在电话里自由交谈时，我就向报社高层编辑坦白了自己的所作所为。出乎意料的是，他们非但没有责备我，反而向我表示祝贺。已经退休的执行总编辑A·M·罗森塔尔私下告诉我，30年前，他曾帮助一名身在共产主义波兰的人秘密逃往西方。《纽约时报》记者悉尼·尚伯格也曾竭尽全力，试图为柬埔寨同事迪斯·普兰伪造护照，帮助他逃过红色高棉的屠杀，虽然最终没有成功。迪斯·普兰后来凭自己的努力逃了出来，在《纽约时报》的新闻编辑部成为了一位深受爱戴的同事。这时刻提醒着我们：除了职业责任，我们还肩负着复杂的人道义务。 There’s nothing I’ve done in my career that was as unprofessional as helping Shawn. But there are also few things I’m prouder of. 在我的整个职业生涯中，没有哪件事比帮助肖恩更不符合职业规范。但也很少有哪件事能让我如此自豪。 纪思道(Nicholas Kristof) 2001起成为时报专栏作家，曾两次获得普利策奖。他最新出版的回忆录名为《追逐希望：一名记者的报道生涯》(“ Chasing Hope: A Reporter’s Life ”)。欢迎在X上关注他： @NickKristof 。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 失言、发怒、关注“屁股”：特朗普的言论变得更粗俗
items.description: PETER BAKER, DYLAN FREEDMAN2026年11月2日 Alex Kent/The New York Times As he opened his speech at a recent campaign rally in Greenville, N.C., President Trump told the story of the Willie Horton crime case that helped sink the presidential campaign of the Democrat Michael S. Dukakis in 1988. 最近在北卡罗来纳州格林维尔一场竞选集会上开场时， 特朗普总统讲述了威利·霍顿的罪案故事。该案件曾在1988年重创民主党人迈克尔·S·杜卡基斯的总统竞选。 And then, 30 minutes later, still speaking at the same rally to the same audience from the same lectern, Mr. Trump told the same Willie Horton story all over again, using some of the same language (and getting the facts wrong both times). 30分钟后，同一场集会、同一群听众、同一个讲台，特朗普又把威利·霍顿的故事讲了一遍，部分措辞与之前相同，而且两次都把事实讲错了。 Mr. Trump, who last year became the oldest person ever inaugurated as president and turned 80 in June, has demonstrated physical stamina as he barnstorms the country in advance of midterm elections. But his performances on the road and at the White House this fall have produced many head-scratching moments that have revived questions about his age and stability. 特朗普去年就职时成为美国历史上年龄最大的总统，今年6月年满80岁。他在中期选举前奔走全国，展现出身体耐力。但今年秋天他在旅途和白宫的表现中出现了许多令人费解的时刻，重新引发了关于他年龄和精神状态的疑问。 He can be forgetful and repetitive. He is more long-winded, more profane and more absolutist than when he ran for president a decade ago. His rambling speeches seem even more garbled at times. He makes comments that leave people wondering what he is talking about or that sound like he is saying something he is not. And even for a president who has never fully observed the norms of the office, he seems more willing to say things no other president would say. 他会健忘，会重复。与十年前竞选总统时相比，他的表达更冗长、更粗俗、更绝对化。他漫无边际的演讲有时变得愈发难以理解。他的一些言论让人摸不着头脑，或者听起来似乎词不达意。即便对于一位从未完全遵循总统职位规范的总统来说，他似乎也更愿意说出其他总统不会说的话。 He declared that at an unfenced construction site “only a Hispanic could survive that fall.” He wants to ban immigrants from Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize.” He says “I don’t give a damn” if he is seen as caring more about oil company profits than struggling workers. He mispronounces the Strait of Hormuz as the “Hormone Strait.” He has told supporters to “cheat like hell” in the Nov. 3 elections. He says military leakers “should be shot.” And then there is his baffling fixation with admiring men’s posteriors. 他声称，在一个没有围栏的建筑工地上，“只有西语裔才能那么摔都没摔死”。他想禁止挪威移民，“因为我没拿到诺贝尔奖”。他说自己“毫不在乎”外界是否认为他更关心石油公司利润而非处境艰难的工人。他把霍尔木兹海峡念成“荷尔蒙海峡”。他让支持者在11月3日的选举中“往死里作弊”。他说军方泄密者“应该被枪毙”。还有他那种欣赏男性臀部的令人费解的执念。 Even Mr. Trump seems astonished at times by what comes out of his mouth — and by how much his supporters embrace him nonetheless. “I could say the stupidest things and you’d clap. ‘Oh, I love you so,’” he marveled at a recent rally in Clarksville, Tenn. “But we don’t say the stupidest things,” he quickly added. “We say things of common sense. We say things that make sense.” 有时连特朗普本人似乎都对自己说出口的话感到惊讶，也对支持者依然如此拥戴他感到惊讶。“我可以说最蠢的话，你们照样鼓掌。‘哦，我好爱你啊，’”他在最近田纳西州克拉克斯维尔的一场集会上感叹道。“但我们不说最蠢的话，”他马上补充道，“我们讲常理。我们说有道理的话。” For Mr. Trump, making sense often places second to having fun at rallies, and some outrageous remarks appear aimed at generating a laugh. His allies say too much is made of comments that are really just jokes. He has always been a provocative speaker, willing to outrage for the sake of outrage. Mr. Trump defends his stream-of-consciousness rambling as a “brilliant” speaking style that he calls “the weave.” 对特朗普来说，讲道理常常要让位于在集会上找乐子，一些出格言论似乎就是为了博人一笑。他的盟友说，那些话其实只是玩笑，外界过度解读了。他一直是个挑衅型演讲者，愿意为激怒而激怒。特朗普为自己意识流式的漫谈辩护，称这是一种他叫做“编织”的“出色”演讲风格。 But the weave seems to be getting weavier. An A.I.-assisted New York Times review of Mr. Trump’s comments from speeches, rallies, social media, interviews and public meetings found significant changes since he began a run for president at age 69 in 2015, although not as much of a notable shift since 2024 when a similar review was conducted. Broadly speaking, the review concluded, Mr. Trump’s public communication is more vulgar, more uninhibited and less coherent than it was a decade ago. 但“编织”似乎越来越“绕”。《纽约时报》借助人工智能查验了特朗普在演讲、集会、社交媒体、采访和公开会议中的言论，发现自他2015年69岁开始竞选总统以来出现了明显变化，不过与2024年进行类似查验时相比变化幅度没有那么显著。总体结论是特朗普的公共表达比十年前更粗俗、更无所顾忌、更缺乏连贯性。 “He’s saying so many stupid things, even for him, so many outrageous and aggressive things,” said former Representative Francis Rooney, a Republican from Florida. “This aggressive kind of attack language, that’s something I’ve never heard from a president.” “他说了太多蠢话，就算按他的标准也太多，太多出格和攻击性的话，”佛罗里达州前共和党众议员弗朗西斯·鲁尼说。“这种攻击性语言，我从未从任何一位总统口中听到过。” The White House denied that Mr. Trump has lost a step. Davis Ingle, a White House spokesman, hailed his “sharpness, unmatched energy, relentless work ethic and historic accessibility” and dismissed concerns about his provocative comments. 白宫否认特朗普精力衰退。白宫发言人戴维斯·英格尔称赞特朗普“敏锐、精力无人能及、工作态度不懈，在可及性上堪称前无古人”，并驳斥了外界对其挑衅性言论的担忧。 “The president doesn’t care about being politically correct, he cares about making America great again,” Mr. Ingle said. “The American people love how authentic, transparent and effective the president is.” “总统不在乎政治正确，他在乎的是让美国再次伟大，”英格尔说。“美国人民热爱总统的真实、透明和高效。” The ‘Freaking Genius’ “十足的天才” 10月，特朗普在亚利桑那州布尔海德市的一场集会上吹嘘自己通过了一项通常用于筛查认知衰退的快速测试。 Measuring the effects of age can be difficult without a medical exam, although that has not stopped many physicians, political commentators and everyday Americans from drawing conclusions about Mr. Trump based on what they see on television. 没有医学检查，很难衡量年龄带来的影响，但这并没有阻止许多医生、政治评论员和普通美国人根据电视上看到的内容对特朗普下结论。 The Times review from 2015 through Thursday found that the president in his second term has used 19 percent more all-or-nothing words like “always,” “never,” “everything” and “totally” at rallies than he did a decade ago and 5 percent more than in 2024, a sign of black-and-white thinking that experts say often accompanies advancing age or cognitive decline. He is cruder than he used to be, using nearly 15 swear words per 10,000 words compared with 14 two years ago and six a decade ago, a change consistent with age-related disinhibition. 《纽约时报》从2015年到本周四的回顾发现，特朗普在第二任期集会上使用“总是”“从不”“一切”“完全”等非黑即白词语的频率比十年前高19%，比2024年高5%。专家说，这种黑白思维往往伴随年龄增长或认知衰退出现。他也比以前更粗鲁，每1万个词中脏话接近15个，两年前为14个，十年前为6个，这一变化符合因年龄增长导致自我抑制力减退（脱抑制）的特征。 The review, relying on an A.I.-assisted metric, found that he makes rambling or confusing digressions in his rallies and speeches two and a half times as often in his second term as in the 2016 campaign, although roughly the same as in 2024. His vocabulary remains about the same, as does the reading level of his speaking, which hovers between fourth and fifth grade. (The average modern president speaks at an eighth-grade level.) 本次回顾采用人工智能辅助指标，发现特朗普在第二任期的集会和演讲中漫无边际或令人困惑的离题频率是2016年竞选期间的2.5倍，但与2024年大致相同。他的词汇量基本没变，演讲的易读性也大致没变，徘徊在四五年级水平。（现代总统的平均演讲水平为八年级。） Mr. Trump’s public schedule is thinner, down to 1.3 events per weekday versus 2.1 in the first term. But he is posting online an average of 21 times a day, up from 13 a day in 2016 although down from 34 a day two years ago. The night owl president has posted messages between midnight and 5 a.m. on 30 percent of his nights in his second term and has had 240 bursts of 10 or more posts an hour. 特朗普的公开日程更稀疏了，从第一任期每个工作日2.1场活动降至1.3场。但他在网上平均每天发帖21次，高于2016年的13次，低于两年前的34次。这位夜猫子总统在第二任期有30%的夜晚在午夜至凌晨5点之间发帖，并有240次在一小时内发帖10条以上。 The president’s doctor has said that Mr. Trump is mentally sharp. In a three-page summary released in May, Dr. Sean P. Barbabella, the White House physician, noted that Mr. Trump had scored 30 out of 30 on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. “Cognitive and physical performance are excellent,” he wrote. 总统的医生表示特朗普头脑敏锐。在5月发布的一份三页摘要中，白宫医生肖恩·P·巴尔巴贝拉指出，特朗普在蒙特利尔认知评估中得分30分，满分30分。“认知和身体表现均出色，”他写道。 The Montreal assessment is a quick test to screen for Alzheimer’s disease or other cognitive impairment and includes basic questions like identifying a lion, camel and rhinoceros; drawing a clock; repeating words or numbers in order; and naming as many words as possible in one minute that start with the letter F. “Nobody can do this,” Mr. Trump insisted a couple weeks ago, adding: “But I can. You know why? Because I’m a freaking genius!” 蒙特利尔评估是一种快速筛查阿尔茨海默病或其他认知障碍的测试，包括辨认狮子、骆驼和犀牛，画钟，按顺序复述词语或数字，以及在一分钟内尽可能多地说出以字母F开头的词等基本题目。“没人做得到这个，”特朗普几周前坚称，随后补充道：“但我能。知道为什么吗？因为我是个十足的天才！” ‘I Don’t Give a Damn’ “我毫不在乎” While Mr. Trump has been known to nod off during White House meetings, he draws energy from crowds when he is on the road. He speaks and speaks and speaks — twice as long as in 2016, according to the Times review, for an average of 85 minutes per rally compared with 42 minutes a decade ago. 特朗普以在白宫会议上打瞌睡而出名，但一到外面就从人群中汲取能量。据时报的回顾，他讲个不停——时长是2016年的两倍，平均每场集会85分钟，十年前为42分钟。 He is profoundly and proudly undisciplined. He says things that are manifestly unhelpful to him. Even as many Americans are upset about the cost of filling their gas tank, he said in Perry, Ga., the other day that high oil prices were good because the fossil fuel industry was making hundreds of billions of dollars. Even as he said it, he acknowledged it would produce bad headlines. “I don’t give a damn,” he said. “I’m going to say it. We’re making a freaking fortune.” 他极度缺乏自律，而且对此引以为豪。他说一些明显对自己不利的话。就在许多美国人为加油成本烦恼之际，他前几天在佐治亚州佩里说，高油价是好事，因为化石燃料行业正在赚取数千亿美元。话一出口，他自己也承认这会带来负面新闻。“我毫不在乎，”他说。“我就是要说。我们正在赚大钱。” He wanders from thought to thought, often without finishing a sentence, embedding one off-the-cuff story within another. In Pendleton, S.C., he started talking about transgender athletes, interrupted to tell a story about someone he met in Israel, referred to a poll without explaining its results and then riffed on climate change. 他从一个念头跳到另一个念头，常常一句话没说完就嵌入另一个即兴故事。在南卡罗来纳州彭德尔顿，他先谈跨性别运动员，中途插进一段在以色列遇到某人的故事，提到一项民调却不解释结果，接着又即兴谈起气候变化。 ‘He’s All Man’ “他是个纯爷们” Like many people in their ninth decade, he is prone to say things that seem inappropriate. His focus on the male anatomy, for instance, has become remarkably pronounced lately. 像许多80多岁的人一样，他容易说一些似乎不合时宜的话。比如，他对男性身体的关注最近变得格外突出。 “I don’t do this with men very often,” Mr. Trump said at a rally with Senator Jon Husted, Republican of Ohio, on Oct. 12. “I started examining his body because I didn’t know he was a great athlete. And I looked and I watched up and down. I looked at his ass.” “我不常对男人这样，”特朗普10月12日在俄亥俄州共和党参议员乔恩·赫斯特德同台的集会上说。“我开始打量他的身体，因为我不知道他是个优秀运动员。我上看下看。我看了他的屁股。” Five days later, he repeated his appreciation of Mr. Husted’s backside. “I examined his ass,” Mr. Trump said at a rally in Kentucky. “I never did that with, no, I never did that with a man before.” Three days later in North Carolina, he praised Mr. Husted’s derrière again. “His ass is, it’s like a pile of muscle,” he said. In Chillicothe, he did it again: “I started by looking at his ass, and it was strong as hell.” 五天后，他又表达了对赫斯特德的臀部的欣赏。“我打量了他的屁股，”特朗普在肯塔基州一场集会上说。“我以前从没这样过，没有，我以前从没对男人这样过。”三天后在北卡罗来纳州，他再次称赞赫斯特德的臀部。“他的屁股，就像一堆肌肉，”他说。在奇利科西，他又来了一次：“我先是看他的屁股，强壮得很。” Mr. Husted is not the only object of Mr. Trump’s manly approval. Among the others: 赫斯特德并非特朗普男性化赞赏的唯一对象。其他还包括： Senator Tim Scott, Republican of South Carolina: “As much as I can fall in love with a man, which isn’t that much, I fall in love with him, and his name happens to be Tim Scott.” 南卡罗来纳州共和党参议员蒂姆·斯科特：“能让我爱上的男人能有几个——没多少——但我爱上了他，他正好叫蒂姆·斯科特。” The spouse of Senator Darline Graham, the other South Carolina Republican: “He’s a good-looking husband.” 另一位南卡罗来纳州共和党参议员达琳·格雷厄姆的配偶：“他是个英俊的丈夫。” Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the health and human services secretary: “He’s got the body of a 30-year-old.” 小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪，卫生与公众服务部长：“他有一副30岁的身体。” Representative Mike Collins, Republican of Georgia: “Mike Collins is a good-looking man. And he’s all man.” 佐治亚州共和党众议员迈克·柯林斯：“迈克·柯林斯是个英俊的男人。而且他是个纯爷们。” In Michigan on Sunday, Mr. Trump made a point of praising a woman’s backside for a change. “I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before — Nicki Minaj,” he told the crowd. “That’s hard to miss.” 周日在密歇根州，特朗普破例夸了一位女性的臀部。“我以前看过一个极其漂亮的屁股——妮琪·米娜，”他告诉人群。“想不注意都难。” A Quick Temper 暴躁易怒 “你是有病吗？”10月20日，在椭圆形办公室被问及东波托马克高尔夫球场项目时，特朗普对一名记者吼道。 Alex Kent/The New York Times Mr. Trump has always displayed fits of public anger in ways that other presidents have not. But he seems even more prone to pounce these days. 特朗普向来会当众发怒，方式与其他总统不同。但他如今似乎更容易突然发难。 He snaps at reporters so often now that he barely waits for their questions before calling them “sick” and ordering, “Quiet!” When a reporter asked on Thursday if he was canceling a trip to Kansas because he was tired of traveling, Mr. Trump accosted his physical appearance. “You are disgusting! Put yourself in shape. You look like hell.” 他现在斥责记者如此频繁，几乎不等对方开口就先骂“有病”，再喝令“安静！”周四，一名记者问他是否因为厌倦出行而取消堪萨斯之行，特朗普转而攻击对方的外貌。“你真恶心！去练练身材。你看起来糟透了。” His exhortations to supporters to vote have grown more vulgar and violent as well. “If you do that,” he said in Vandalia, Ohio, “we’re going to win and we’re going to win big. And we’re going to shove it up their ass, OK?” 他对支持者投票的鼓动也变得更粗俗、更暴力。“你们要是这么做，”他在俄亥俄州万达利亚说，“我们就会赢，会大赢。咱们就给它塞他们的屁股里，是吧？” He depicts himself as all-powerful. “I can do whatever I want,” he told reporters in the Oval Office recently. As if to prove it, he regularly tries to rename bodies of water after America or himself. He demanded that tech companies stop using the term artificial intelligence, preferring instead “super intelligence”; those that disobey, he wrote online, are “THE ENEMY!” 他把自己描绘成无所不能。“我想做什么就做什么，”他最近在椭圆形办公室对记者说。仿佛为了证明这一点，他经常试图以美国或自己的名字重新命名水域。他要求科技公司停止使用“人工智能”一词，改用“超级智能”；他在网上写道，不服从的公司就是“敌人！” These days, even Mr. Trump seems aware that eyes are on him, watching and waiting. “I love the weave,” he told the midterm Republican convention in Dallas in September. “You know what the weave is? You talk about something, then you bring in a ballroom or you bring in an airplane or you bring in Air Force One. But you notice I always get right back to the same topic.” 如今，连特朗普本人似乎也意识到大家都在盯着他，看他会有什么表现。“我喜欢编织，”他9月在达拉斯对中期共和党大会说。“知道什么是编织吗？你谈一件事，然后扯进一个宴会厅，或者一架飞机，或者空军一号。但你会发现我总是回到同一个话题。” And yet, he went on, “when someday, there’ll be a time when I do the weave is weave, weave. Someday, there’ll be a time when I don’t get back to the original subject, and then you can say he’s had it. OK? You can say then he’s had it.” 但他接着说，“总有一天，会有一个时候，我编织起来就是编织、编织、编织。总有一天，会有一个时候，我没回到最初的话题，那时候你们就可以说他不行了。好吗？到时候你们就可以说他不行了。” 方法论 时报利用Roll Call的Factba.se从2015年到今年10月下旬的数据，收集了特朗普数千份演讲、采访、社交媒体帖子和日程。为量化特朗普对非黑即白语言和脏话的使用，我们统计了他各总统任期和竞选期间的基本词频。为识别令人困惑和漫无边际的段落，我们使用人工智能模型Claude Opus 5.5，根据我们此前报道中分析特朗普漫谈和粗俗语言的详细指引，对超过6500段特朗普演讲进行评分。按照这套评分标准——它基于对数百段文字的人工审查以及为确保高准确性所做的评估——一段演讲得分至少达到七分（满分10分），即计为不连贯。 Peter Baker是《纽约时报》首席白宫记者。特朗普是他报道的第六任美国总统，有时他也撰写将总统和美国政府置于更宏观的背景和历史框架下的分析性文章。 Dylan Freedman是时报人工智能项目编辑，负责调查各种相关话题。他既有记者经验，也有机器学习工程师经验。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
items.content: PETER BAKER, DYLAN FREEDMAN 2026年11月2日 Alex Kent/The New York Times As he opened his speech at a recent campaign rally in Greenville, N.C., President Trump told the story of the Willie Horton crime case that helped sink the presidential campaign of the Democrat Michael S. Dukakis in 1988. 最近在北卡罗来纳州格林维尔一场竞选集会上开场时， 特朗普总统讲述了威利·霍顿的罪案故事。该案件曾在1988年重创民主党人迈克尔·S·杜卡基斯的总统竞选。 And then, 30 minutes later, still speaking at the same rally to the same audience from the same lectern, Mr. Trump told the same Willie Horton story all over again, using some of the same language (and getting the facts wrong both times). 30分钟后，同一场集会、同一群听众、同一个讲台，特朗普 又把威利·霍顿的故事讲了一遍 ，部分措辞与之前相同，而且两次都把事实讲错了。 Mr. Trump, who last year became the oldest person ever inaugurated as president and turned 80 in June, has demonstrated physical stamina as he barnstorms the country in advance of midterm elections. But his performances on the road and at the White House this fall have produced many head-scratching moments that have revived questions about his age and stability . 特朗普去年就职时成为 美国历史上年龄最大的总统 ，今年6月年满80岁。他在中期选举前奔走全国，展现出身体耐力。但今年秋天他在旅途和白宫的表现中出现了许多令人费解的时刻，重新引发了 关于他年龄和精神状态的疑问 。 He can be forgetful and repetitive. He is more long-winded, more profane and more absolutist than when he ran for president a decade ago. His rambling speeches seem even more garbled at times. He makes comments that leave people wondering what he is talking about or that sound like he is saying something he is not. And even for a president who has never fully observed the norms of the office, he seems more willing to say things no other president would say. 他会健忘，会重复。与十年前竞选总统时相比，他的表达更冗长、更粗俗、更绝对化。他漫无边际的演讲有时变得愈发难以理解。他的一些言论让人摸不着头脑，或者听起来似乎词不达意。即便对于一位从未完全遵循总统职位规范的总统来说，他似乎也更愿意说出其他总统不会说的话。 He declared that at an unfenced construction site “only a Hispanic could survive that fall.” He wants to ban immigrants from Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize.” He says “I don’t give a damn” if he is seen as caring more about oil company profits than struggling workers. He mispronounces the Strait of Hormuz as the “Hormone Strait.” He has told supporters to “cheat like hell” in the Nov. 3 elections. He says military leakers “should be shot.” And then there is his baffling fixation with admiring men’s posteriors . 他声称，在一个没有围栏的建筑工地上， “只有西语裔才能那么摔都没摔死” 。他想禁止挪威移民， “因为我没拿到诺贝尔奖” 。他说自己 “毫不在乎” 外界是否认为他更关心石油公司利润而非处境艰难的工人。他把霍尔木兹海峡念成“荷尔蒙海峡”。他让支持者在11月3日的选举中 “往死里作弊” 。他说军方泄密者 “应该被枪毙” 。还有他那种 欣赏男性臀部 的令人费解的执念。 Even Mr. Trump seems astonished at times by what comes out of his mouth — and by how much his supporters embrace him nonetheless. “I could say the stupidest things and you’d clap. ‘Oh, I love you so,’” he marveled at a recent rally in Clarksville, Tenn. “But we don’t say the stupidest things,” he quickly added. “We say things of common sense. We say things that make sense.” 有时连特朗普本人似乎都对自己说出口的话感到惊讶，也对支持者依然如此拥戴他感到惊讶。“我可以说最蠢的话，你们照样鼓掌。‘哦，我好爱你啊，’”他在最近 田纳西州克拉克斯维尔 的一场集会上感叹道。“但我们不说最蠢的话，”他马上补充道，“我们讲常理。我们说有道理的话。” For Mr. Trump, making sense often places second to having fun at rallies, and some outrageous remarks appear aimed at generating a laugh. His allies say too much is made of comments that are really just jokes. He has always been a provocative speaker, willing to outrage for the sake of outrage. Mr. Trump defends his stream-of-consciousness rambling as a “brilliant” speaking style that he calls “the weave.” 对特朗普来说，讲道理常常要让位于在集会上找乐子，一些出格言论似乎就是为了博人一笑。他的盟友说，那些话其实只是玩笑，外界过度解读了。他一直是个挑衅型演讲者，愿意为激怒而激怒。特朗普为自己意识流式的漫谈辩护，称这是一种他叫做 “编织” 的“出色”演讲风格。 But the weave seems to be getting weavier. An A.I.-assisted New York Times review of Mr. Trump’s comments from speeches, rallies, social media, interviews and public meetings found significant changes since he began a run for president at age 69 in 2015, although not as much of a notable shift since 2024 when a similar review was conducted . Broadly speaking, the review concluded, Mr. Trump’s public communication is more vulgar, more uninhibited and less coherent than it was a decade ago. 但“编织”似乎越来越“绕”。《纽约时报》借助人工智能查验了特朗普在演讲、集会、社交媒体、采访和公开会议中的言论，发现自他2015年69岁开始竞选总统以来出现了明显变化，不过与2024年 进行类似查验 时相比变化幅度没有那么显著。总体结论是特朗普的公共表达比十年前更粗俗、更无所顾忌、更缺乏连贯性。 “He’s saying so many stupid things, even for him, so many outrageous and aggressive things,” said former Representative Francis Rooney, a Republican from Florida. “This aggressive kind of attack language, that’s something I’ve never heard from a president.” “他说了太多蠢话，就算按他的标准也太多，太多出格和攻击性的话，”佛罗里达州前共和党众议员弗朗西斯·鲁尼说。“这种攻击性语言，我从未从任何一位总统口中听到过。” The White House denied that Mr. Trump has lost a step. Davis Ingle, a White House spokesman, hailed his “sharpness, unmatched energy, relentless work ethic and historic accessibility” and dismissed concerns about his provocative comments. 白宫否认特朗普精力衰退。白宫发言人戴维斯·英格尔称赞特朗普“敏锐、精力无人能及、工作态度不懈，在可及性上堪称前无古人”，并驳斥了外界对其挑衅性言论的担忧。 “The president doesn’t care about being politically correct, he cares about making America great again,” Mr. Ingle said. “The American people love how authentic, transparent and effective the president is.” “总统不在乎政治正确，他在乎的是让美国再次伟大，”英格尔说。“美国人民热爱总统的真实、透明和高效。” The ‘Freaking Genius’ “十足的天才” 10月，特朗普在亚利桑那州布尔海德市的一场集会上吹嘘自己通过了一项通常用于筛查认知衰退的快速测试。 Measuring the effects of age can be difficult without a medical exam, although that has not stopped many physicians, political commentators and everyday Americans from drawing conclusions about Mr. Trump based on what they see on television. 没有医学检查，很难衡量年龄带来的影响，但这并没有阻止许多医生、政治评论员和普通美国人根据电视上看到的内容对特朗普下结论。 The Times review from 2015 through Thursday found that the president in his second term has used 19 percent more all-or-nothing words like “always,” “never,” “everything” and “totally” at rallies than he did a decade ago and 5 percent more than in 2024, a sign of black-and-white thinking that experts say often accompanies advancing age or cognitive decline. He is cruder than he used to be, using nearly 15 swear words per 10,000 words compared with 14 two years ago and six a decade ago, a change consistent with age-related disinhibition. 《纽约时报》从2015年到本周四的回顾发现，特朗普在第二任期集会上使用“总是”“从不”“一切”“完全”等非黑即白词语的频率比十年前高19%，比2024年高5%。专家说，这种黑白思维往往伴随年龄增长或认知衰退出现。他也比以前更粗鲁，每1万个词中脏话接近15个，两年前为14个，十年前为6个，这一变化符合因年龄增长导致自我抑制力减退（脱抑制）的特征。 The review, relying on an A.I.-assisted metric, found that he makes rambling or confusing digressions in his rallies and speeches two and a half times as often in his second term as in the 2016 campaign, although roughly the same as in 2024. His vocabulary remains about the same, as does the reading level of his speaking, which hovers between fourth and fifth grade. (The average modern president speaks at an eighth-grade level.) 本次回顾采用人工智能辅助指标，发现特朗普在第二任期的集会和演讲中漫无边际或令人困惑的离题频率是2016年竞选期间的2.5倍，但与2024年大致相同。他的词汇量基本没变，演讲的易读性也大致没变，徘徊在四五年级水平。（现代总统的平均演讲水平为八年级。） Mr. Trump’s public schedule is thinner, down to 1.3 events per weekday versus 2.1 in the first term. But he is posting online an average of 21 times a day, up from 13 a day in 2016 although down from 34 a day two years ago. The night owl president has posted messages between midnight and 5 a.m. on 30 percent of his nights in his second term and has had 240 bursts of 10 or more posts an hour. 特朗普的公开日程更稀疏了，从第一任期每个工作日2.1场活动降至1.3场。但他在网上平均每天发帖21次，高于2016年的13次，低于两年前的34次。这位夜猫子总统在第二任期有30%的夜晚在午夜至凌晨5点之间发帖，并有240次在一小时内发帖10条以上。 The president’s doctor has said that Mr. Trump is mentally sharp. In a three-page summary released in May, Dr. Sean P. Barbabella, the White House physician, noted that Mr. Trump had scored 30 out of 30 on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. “Cognitive and physical performance are excellent,” he wrote. 总统的医生表示特朗普头脑敏锐。在5月发布的 一份三页摘要 中，白宫医生肖恩·P·巴尔巴贝拉指出，特朗普在蒙特利尔认知评估中得分30分，满分30分。“认知和身体表现均出色，”他写道。 The Montreal assessment is a quick test to screen for Alzheimer’s disease or other cognitive impairment and includes basic questions like identifying a lion, camel and rhinoceros; drawing a clock; repeating words or numbers in order; and naming as many words as possible in one minute that start with the letter F. “Nobody can do this,” Mr. Trump insisted a couple weeks ago, adding: “But I can. You know why? Because I’m a freaking genius!” 蒙特利尔评估 是一种快速筛查阿尔茨海默病或其他认知障碍的测试，包括辨认狮子、骆驼和犀牛，画钟，按顺序复述词语或数字，以及在一分钟内尽可能多地说出以字母F开头的词等基本题目。“没人做得到这个，”特朗普几周前坚称，随后补充道：“但我能。知道为什么吗？因为我是个十足的天才！” ‘I Don’t Give a Damn’ “我毫不在乎” While Mr. Trump has been known to nod off during White House meetings, he draws energy from crowds when he is on the road. He speaks and speaks and speaks — twice as long as in 2016, according to the Times review, for an average of 85 minutes per rally compared with 42 minutes a decade ago. 特朗普以在白宫会议上打瞌睡而出名，但一到外面就从人群中汲取能量。据时报的回顾，他讲个不停——时长是2016年的两倍，平均每场集会85分钟，十年前为42分钟。 He is profoundly and proudly undisciplined. He says things that are manifestly unhelpful to him. Even as many Americans are upset about the cost of filling their gas tank, he said in Perry, Ga., the other day that high oil prices were good because the fossil fuel industry was making hundreds of billions of dollars. Even as he said it, he acknowledged it would produce bad headlines. “I don’t give a damn,” he said. “I’m going to say it. We’re making a freaking fortune.” 他极度缺乏自律，而且对此引以为豪。他说一些明显对自己不利的话。就在许多美国人为加油成本烦恼之际，他前几天在 佐治亚州佩里 说，高油价是好事，因为化石燃料行业正在赚取数千亿美元。话一出口，他自己也承认这会带来负面新闻。“我毫不在乎，”他说。“我就是要说。我们正在赚大钱。” He wanders from thought to thought, often without finishing a sentence, embedding one off-the-cuff story within another. In Pendleton, S.C., he started talking about transgender athletes, interrupted to tell a story about someone he met in Israel, referred to a poll without explaining its results and then riffed on climate change. 他从一个念头跳到另一个念头，常常一句话没说完就嵌入另一个即兴故事。 在南卡罗来纳州彭德尔顿 ，他先谈跨性别运动员，中途插进一段在以色列遇到某人的故事，提到一项民调却不解释结果，接着又即兴谈起气候变化。 ‘He’s All Man’ “他是 个纯爷们 ” Like many people in their ninth decade, he is prone to say things that seem inappropriate. His focus on the male anatomy, for instance, has become remarkably pronounced lately. 像许多80多岁的人一样，他容易说一些似乎不合时宜的话。比如，他对男性身体的关注最近变得 格外突出 。 “I don’t do this with men very often,” Mr. Trump said at a rally with Senator Jon Husted, Republican of Ohio, on Oct. 12. “I started examining his body because I didn’t know he was a great athlete. And I looked and I watched up and down. I looked at his ass.” “我不常对男人这样，”特朗普10月12日在俄亥俄州共和党参议员乔恩·赫斯特德同台的 集会上说 。“我开始打量他的身体，因为我不知道他是个优秀运动员。我上看下看。我看了他的屁股。” Five days later, he repeated his appreciation of Mr. Husted’s backside. “I examined his ass,” Mr. Trump said at a rally in Kentucky . “I never did that with, no, I never did that with a man before.” Three days later in North Carolina , he praised Mr. Husted’s derrière again. “His ass is, it’s like a pile of muscle,” he said. In Chillicothe , he did it again: “I started by looking at his ass, and it was strong as hell.” 五天后，他又表达了对赫斯特德的臀部的欣赏。“我打量了他的屁股，”特朗普在 肯塔基州一场集会 上说。“我以前从没这样过，没有，我以前从没对男人这样过。”三天后 在北卡罗来纳州 ，他再次称赞赫斯特德的臀部。“他的屁股，就像一堆肌肉，”他说。 在奇利科西 ，他又来了一次：“我先是看他的屁股，强壮得很。” Mr. Husted is not the only object of Mr. Trump’s manly approval. Among the others: 赫斯特德并非特朗普男性化赞赏的唯一对象。其他还包括： Senator Tim Scott , Republican of South Carolina: “As much as I can fall in love with a man, which isn’t that much, I fall in love with him, and his name happens to be Tim Scott.” 南卡罗来纳州共和党参议员 蒂姆·斯科特 ：“能让我爱上的男人能有几个——没多少——但我爱上了他，他正好叫蒂姆·斯科特。” The spouse of Senator Darline Graham , the other South Carolina Republican: “He’s a good-looking husband.” 另一位南卡罗来纳州共和党参议员 达琳·格雷厄姆 的配偶：“他是个英俊的丈夫。” Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the health and human services secretary: “He’s got the body of a 30-year-old.” 小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 ，卫生与公众服务部长：“他有一副30岁的身体。” Representative Mike Collins , Republican of Georgia: “Mike Collins is a good-looking man. And he’s all man.” 佐治亚州共和党众议员 迈克·柯林斯 ：“迈克·柯林斯是个英俊的男人。而且他是个纯爷们。” In Michigan on Sunday, Mr. Trump made a point of praising a woman’s backside for a change. “I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before — Nicki Minaj,” he told the crowd. “That’s hard to miss.” 周日在密歇根州，特朗普破例夸了一位女性的臀部。“我以前看过一个极其漂亮的屁股——妮琪·米娜，”他告诉人群。“想不注意都难。” A Quick Temper 暴躁易怒 “你是有病吗？”10月20日，在椭圆形办公室被问及东波托马克高尔夫球场项目时，特朗普对一名记者吼道。 Alex Kent/The New York Times Mr. Trump has always displayed fits of public anger in ways that other presidents have not. But he seems even more prone to pounce these days. 特朗普向来会当众发怒，方式与其他总统不同。但他如今似乎更容易突然发难。 He snaps at reporters so often now that he barely waits for their questions before calling them “sick” and ordering, “Quiet!” When a reporter asked on Thursday if he was canceling a trip to Kansas because he was tired of traveling, Mr. Trump accosted his physical appearance. “You are disgusting! Put yourself in shape. You look like hell.” 他现在斥责记者如此频繁，几乎不等对方开口就先骂“有病”，再喝令“安静！”周四，一名记者问他是否因为厌倦出行而取消堪萨斯之行，特朗普转而攻击对方的外貌。“你真恶心！去练练身材。你看起来糟透了。” His exhortations to supporters to vote have grown more vulgar and violent as well. “If you do that,” he said in Vandalia, Ohio , “we’re going to win and we’re going to win big. And we’re going to shove it up their ass, OK?” 他对支持者投票的鼓动也变得更粗俗、更暴力。“你们要是这么做，”他在 俄亥俄州万达利亚 说，“我们就会赢，会大赢。咱们就给它塞他们的屁股里，是吧？” He depicts himself as all-powerful. “I can do whatever I want,” he told reporters in the Oval Office recently. As if to prove it, he regularly tries to rename bodies of water after America or himself. He demanded that tech companies stop using the term artificial intelligence, preferring instead “super intelligence”; those that disobey, he wrote online, are “THE ENEMY!” 他把自己描绘成无所不能。“我想做什么就做什么，”他最近在椭圆形办公室对记者说。仿佛为了证明这一点，他经常试图以美国或自己的名字重新命名水域。他要求科技公司停止使用“人工智能”一词，改用“超级智能”；他在网上写道，不服从的公司就是 “敌人！” These days, even Mr. Trump seems aware that eyes are on him, watching and waiting. “I love the weave,” he told the midterm Republican convention in Dallas in September. “You know what the weave is? You talk about something, then you bring in a ballroom or you bring in an airplane or you bring in Air Force One. But you notice I always get right back to the same topic.” 如今，连特朗普本人似乎也意识到大家都在盯着他，看他会有什么表现。“我喜欢编织，”他9月 在达拉斯对中期共和党大会 说。“知道什么是编织吗？你谈一件事，然后扯进一个宴会厅，或者一架飞机，或者空军一号。但你会发现我总是回到同一个话题。” And yet, he went on, “when someday, there’ll be a time when I do the weave is weave, weave. Someday, there’ll be a time when I don’t get back to the original subject, and then you can say he’s had it. OK? You can say then he’s had it.” 但他接着说，“总有一天，会有一个时候，我编织起来就是编织、编织、编织。总有一天，会有一个时候，我没回到最初的话题，那时候你们就可以说他不行了。好吗？到时候你们就可以说他不行了。” 方法论 时报利用 Roll Call的Factba.se 从2015年到今年10月下旬的数据，收集了特朗普数千份演讲、采访、社交媒体帖子和日程。为量化特朗普对非黑即白语言和脏话的使用，我们统计了他各总统任期和竞选期间的基本词频。为识别令人困惑和漫无边际的段落，我们使用人工智能模型Claude Opus 5.5，根据我们 此前报道 中分析特朗普漫谈和粗俗语言的详细指引，对超过6500段特朗普演讲进行评分。按照这套评分标准——它基于对数百段文字的人工审查以及为确保高准确性所做的评估——一段演讲得分至少达到七分（满分10分），即计为不连贯。 Peter Baker 是《纽约时报》首席白宫记者。特朗普是他报道的第六任美国总统，有时他也撰写将总统和美国政府置于更宏观的背景和历史框架下的分析性文章。 Dylan Freedman 是时报人工智能项目编辑，负责调查各种相关话题。他既有记者经验，也有机器学习工程师经验。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 币安63亿美元黑客攻击事件始末
items.description: DAVID YAFFE-BELLANY2026年11月2日全球最大加密货币交易所币安表示，这起被业内称为史上最大规模加密货币黑客攻击的事件涉及约63亿美元资金。 SeongJoon Cho/Bloomberg At about 4:20 p.m. on Thursday, a string of unusual transactions started to cause alarm at Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange. 周四下午4点20分左右，一连串异常交易开始引起全球最大加密货币交易所币安的警觉。 Money was pouring out of the company’s accounts, a multibillion-dollar deluge of digital coins. It had all the hallmarks of a crypto heist — a high-speed bank robbery conducted over the internet. 资金正从公司的账户中大量流出，价值数十亿美元的数字货币如洪水般倾泻而去。种种迹象都表明，这是一场加密货币盗窃案——一场在互联网上高速进行的银行抢劫。 As the news spread, Binance’s top executives put together an informal war room on Wea, the company’s internal messaging system, with about 100 participants, including specialized cryptocurrency tracers and security personnel. 随着消息传开，币安高管在公司内部通讯系统Wea上临时组建起一个危机应对群组，约有100人参与，其中包括专门追踪加密货币流向的专家和安全人员。 They eventually transitioned to a mass conference call, with 100 boxes on the screen, where employees took turns muting and then unmuting, communicating in a mixture of English and Chinese. Among them was He Yi, Binance’s co-chief executive, who is seven months pregnant, and worked through the night from her base in Abu Dhabi, taking a call at 3 a.m. local time. 后来，他们转而召开大型电话会议，屏幕上显示着100个视频窗口。员工们轮流关闭和打开麦克风，时而说英语，时而说中文。参与者中包括币安联席首席执行官何一。怀孕七个月的她在阿布扎比的办公地点彻夜工作，当地时间凌晨3点还在接听电话。 Ms. He and her colleagues were navigating one of the most damaging crises in Binance’s long and troubled history. A team of North Korean hackers had penetrated the exchange and drained more than $6 billion in the largest crypto heist of all time. Binance was forced to halt deposits and withdrawals, and posted a series of frantic messages on X, promising that it would cover any losses. 何一和她的同事们正在应对币安漫长而风波不断的历史上最具破坏性的危机之一。一个朝鲜黑客团队侵入了这家交易所，盗走逾60亿美元，制造了有史以来规模最大的加密货币盗窃案。币安被迫暂停充值和提现，并在X平台上发布一系列措辞急切的消息，承诺承担所有损失。 It was a surreal situation made even more surreal by the actions of Binance’s founder, Changpeng Zhao, who spent the evening narrating the events to his 12.9 million followers on X. He posted prayer hand emojis, publicly jousted with the site’s owner, Elon Musk, and insisted that “user funds are SAFU” — using a bit of crypto slang to reassure customers that hundreds of millions of dollars in deposits would not simply vanish into thin air. 这场危机本已令人难以置信，而币安创始人赵长鹏的举动又给它增添了几分超现实色彩。他整晚都在X平台上向自己的1290万名粉丝实时讲述事态进展。他发布双手合十的表情符号，与X平台所有者埃隆·马斯克公开交锋，还坚称“用户资金SAFU”，这是借用币圈的行话向客户保证，他们数亿美元的存款不会凭空消失。 “It hurts, but we will survive,” Mr. Zhao declared. “这很痛苦，但我们会挺过去的。”赵长鹏宣称。 币安创始人赵长鹏，摄于8月。黑客攻击当晚，他通宵在X上向1290万粉丝描述事件进展。 The impact of the Binance attack rippled across the crypto industry, from Abu Dhabi to New York, setting off a frantic effort to salvage some of the stolen funds and prompting law enforcement inquiries. This account of how the hack unfolded is based on interviews with four people with knowledge of the events, as well as analyses by crypto forensics firms and documents reviewed by The New York Times. 币安遭受攻击的影响波及整个加密货币行业，从阿布扎比到纽约，各方慌忙采取紧急行动，试图追回部分被盗资金，也促使执法机构开始介入调查。基于对四名知情人士的采访、加密货币取证公司的分析，以及《纽约时报》查阅的相关文件，本文对这场黑客攻击经过进行了还原。 For years, Binance has been the most important and contentious company in the crypto world. After Mr. Zhao founded it in 2017, it quickly turned into a behemoth, the No. 1 destination for customers looking to convert traditional currencies into digital coins like Bitcoin and Ether. 多年来，币安一直是币圈最重要也最具争议的公司。赵长鹏2017年创立币安后，该公司迅速发展成为行业巨头，成为希望将传统货币兑换成比特币、以太币等数字货币的客户首选平台。 It also became a haven for crime. In 2023, Binance pleaded guilty to anti-money-laundering violations that had allowed criminals to move money and paid $4.3 billion in penalties to U.S. regulators. Mr. Zhao was sentenced to four months in prison. 但币安也成了犯罪活动的温床。2023年，币安承认违反反洗钱规定，致使犯罪分子得以通过其平台转移资金，并向美国监管机构支付了43亿美元罚款。赵长鹏被判处四个月监禁。 For all its troubles, however, Binance never lost popularity among the crypto faithful. It remains the world’s largest exchange by a distance, and Mr. Zhao, who lives in Abu Dhabi, is something of an industry folk hero. Binance’s main platform is banned in the United States. But last year, the company forged a business relationship with World Liberty Financial, the Trump family crypto start-up. President Trump granted a pardon to Mr. Zhao last October, paving the way for Binance to expand into the U.S. market. 尽管麻烦不断，币安在加密货币忠实拥趸中的人气却始终不减。它仍然以遥遥领先的优势稳居全球最大加密货币交易所的地位，而居住在阿布扎比的赵长鹏在业内俨然是一位民间英雄。币安的主要交易平台在美国被禁，但去年，该公司与特朗普家族创办的加密货币初创企业世界自由金融公司建立了业务关系。去年10月，特朗普总统赦免了赵长鹏，为币安拓展美国市场铺平了道路。 But on the night of Oct. 29, the company had to deal with the aftermath of the $6 billion hack. 然而，10月29日夜里，币安不得不面对这场60亿美元黑客攻击造成的后果。 Such attacks have become commonplace in the crypto world. In February 2025, the North Koreans stole $1.5 billion from Bybit, a rival exchange. Bybit was breached after Ben Zhou, its chief executive, approved a seemingly routine transaction that granted the thieves access to the exchange’s internal system. 此类攻击在加密货币领域已司空见惯。2025年2月，朝鲜人从币安的竞争对手Bybit盗走15亿美元。Bybit被入侵是因为其首席执行官周雨辰批准了一笔看似常规的交易，使窃贼得以进入交易所内部系统。 It’s not clear precisely how the North Koreans got around Binance’s defenses. An initial investigation pointed to a compromised laptop, Binance said Friday. But the company later said it had uncovered “additional points of breach.” 目前尚不清楚朝鲜黑客究竟是如何突破了币安的防御系统。币安周五表示，初步调查指向一台遭到入侵的笔记本电脑。但该公司后来又称，发现了“更多入侵点”。 Much of the drama played out in public. Almost all crypto transactions are recorded on the blockchain, a ledger of money movements that anyone can look up. That meant crypto analysts could see funds leaving Binance in real time. 这场危机的许多情节都在公众眼皮底下上演。几乎所有加密货币交易都会记录在区块链上，这是一套任何人都可以查询的资金流动账本。这意味着，加密货币分析师能够实时看到资金从币安流出。 On Thursday afternoon, Jonathan Levin, the chief executive of the crypto analytics firm Chainalysis, was on a video call with a former senior U.S. official, discussing the need for the U.S. government to deploy cyber attacks against adversaries. Then Mr. Levin got the news about Binance. 周四下午，加密货币分析公司Chainalysis首席执行官乔纳森·莱文正在与一名前美国高级官员视频通话，讨论美国政府有必要对敌对势力动用网络攻击手段。就在这时，莱文收到了币安遭到攻击的消息。 “I looked at my phone and was like, ‘Oh, this doesn’t look good,’” he said in an interview. “我看了一眼手机，心想，‘哦，情况看起来不妙。’”他在接受采访时说。 A group of Chainalysis employees gathered in a conference room in New York named “Silk Road,” after another crypto platform that was famously hacked. They worked until the early hours of Friday morning, eating Malaysian food and analyzing transactions to get a clearer picture of what had happened. 一群Chainalysis员工聚集在纽约一间名为“丝绸之路”的会议室里。这个名字来自另一个曾因遭到黑客攻击而闻名的加密货币平台。他们一边吃着马来西亚菜，一边分析交易记录，一直工作到周五凌晨，试图进一步厘清究竟发生了什么。 Soon both Chainalysis and another analytics firm, TRM Labs, attributed the attack to an elite North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. The F.B.I. confirmed their findings. North Koreans have targeted crypto companies for years, using the proceeds of those thefts to fund its nuclear program, according to Western officials. 不久，Chainalysis和另一家分析公司TRM Labs都认定，这次攻击出自朝鲜一个名为TraderTraitor的精锐黑客组织。美国联邦调查局证实了他们的调查结果。西方官员表示，朝鲜多年来一直将加密货币公司作为攻击目标，并利用窃取的资金资助其核武器计划。 The hackers have developed increasingly complex strategies to steal crypto and launder the proceeds, a painstaking endeavor that can take months to complete. In a blog post on Friday, Chainalysis said the attackers had deployed “laundering patterns we have not seen before,” conducting thousands of transactions over a short period, probably with the help of automation. 黑客们开发出越来越复杂的策略来窃取加密货币并洗白收益，这一过程十分繁琐，可能需要数月才能完成。Chainalysis周五在一篇博客文章中说，攻击者使用了“我们从未见过的洗钱模式”，在短时间内进行数千笔交易，可能借助了自动化工具。 At the same time, Binance’s colleagues in the industry mobilized to intercept some of the laundered crypto. Certain digital coin issuers can freeze funds, allowing them to halt a money-laundering operation in its tracks. 与此同时，币安的行业同行也行动起来，试图拦截部分被洗白的加密货币。某些数字货币发行方可以冻结资金，从而及时阻止洗钱操作。 Soon after the hack, Tether and Circle, two major issuers, announced that they had frozen stashes of their own coins that the hackers had seized from Binance, a combined total of more than $2 billion in crypto. Binance is now working to gain access to those funds, the company said. 黑客攻击发生后不久，两家主要数字货币发行商Tether和Circle宣布，已冻结黑客从币安窃取的部分由它们发行的数字货币，总价值超过20亿美元。币安表示，目前正设法重新取得这些资金的控制权。 But $2.4 billion in crypto is already “beyond any issuer’s reach,” according to TRM. In a social media post on Friday, Binance said that it had set aside $6.34 billion to cover losses from the hack. 但TRM指出，已有价值24亿美元的加密货币“超出了任何发行商能够控制的范围”。币安周五在社交媒体发文称，已拨出63.4亿美元，用于弥补此次黑客攻击造成的损失。 How much money Binance has in reserve is not publicly known. After midnight, Mr. Musk posted a grimacing emoji underneath an X post comparing Mr. Zhao to Sam Bankman-Fried, the disgraced crypto mogul whose FTX exchange collapsed in 2022. 币安究竟持有多少储备资金，外界并不清楚。午夜过后，马斯克在一条将赵长鹏比作萨姆·班克曼-弗里德的X帖子下发布了一个龇牙表情；后者是声名狼藉的加密巨头，其创办的FTX交易所于2022年倒闭。 “Bad time to troll,” Mr. Zhao responded. “Please stop.” He noted that Binance owns over $1 billion in shares in SpaceX, Mr. Musk’s rocket company. “现在不是起哄的时候，”赵长鹏回应道。“请住手。”他指出，币安持有马斯克火箭公司SpaceX超过10亿美元的股份。 赵长鹏周五在X上与埃隆·马斯克打起了口水仗。 Mr. Zhao’s comment got the attention of Ms. He, Binance’s co-chief executive and his longtime romantic partner. (Mr. Zhao is Binance’s majority shareholder but doesn’t have a formal role at the company.) 赵长鹏的这番话引起了币安联席首席执行官何一的注意。何一也是他多年的伴侣。（赵长鹏是币安的控股股东，但并未在公司担任正式职务。） “Our company’s revenue for the year is sufficient to cover the losses, so we do not yet need to sell the SpaceX shares,” Ms. He wrote. “我们公司今年的收入足以覆盖这次损失，因此目前还不需要出售SpaceX的股份。”何一写道。 With the industry reeling, Ms. He and her co-chief executive, Richard Teng, told Binance employees to “stay disciplined,” according to a message reviewed by The Times. 据《纽约时报》看到的一条内部信息，在行业震荡之际，何一和联合首席执行官邓伟政要求币安员工要“严守纪律”。 "Do not speculate internally or externally,” the message said. “We know this is an intense moment, and we deeply appreciate everyone working overtime to make this right.” “无论在公司内外，都不要妄加猜测，”信息写道。“我们知道现在形势严峻，非常感谢大家加班加点，努力解决问题。” They also tried to address the growing unease in the crypto world. Speaking in Mandarin in a video posted to X on Friday, Ms. He said that the rise of artificial intelligence had turned hacking into “a threat to the entire industry.” 他们还试图回应币圈日益加剧的不安。周五在X发布的一段视频中，何一用普通话表示，人工智能的兴起已使黑客攻击成为“整个行业的威胁”。 “Of course, there are many things that we have done wrong,” she said. “We should have invested in security much earlier and more extensively, and established more rigorous standards.” “当然，我们也有很多做得不对的地方。”她说，“我们应该更早地、更多地去做安全投入，建立更严谨的标准。” Word of Binance’s hack even reached Mr. Trump, who was asked about it by a reporter on Friday. “People never see the money anymore,” he said. “I’ve always felt it was a little bit dangerous. But they say they have it pretty much under control. We’ll see.” 币安被攻击的消息甚至传到了特朗普那里，周五有记者问及此事。“人们再也看不到钱了，”他说。“我一直觉得这有点危险。但他们说基本控制住了。我们拭目以待。” Among the companies that rushed to Binance’s aid was the Trump family firm, World Liberty, the issuer of a coin known as USD1. 在迅速向币安伸出援手的公司中，包括特朗普家族的世界自由金融。这家公司发行了一种名为USD1的数字货币。 Zach Witkoff, the company’s chief executive and the son of one of Mr. Trump’s top advisers, announced on X that World Liberty had frozen $27 million in USD1 that was “associated with the Binance hack.” 该公司首席执行官扎克·威特科夫是特朗普一名高级顾问的儿子。他在X平台宣布，世界自由金融已冻结价值2700万美元与“币安黑客攻击事件有关”的USD1。 “We stand by our industry partners,” he wrote. “我们坚定支持业内合作伙伴。”他写道。 “Thank you!” Mr. Zhao responded, followed by three prayer hand emojis. “谢谢！”赵长鹏回复道，后面跟着三个双手合十的表情符号。 傅才德(Michael Forsythe)和Dustin Volz对本文有报道贡献。 David Yaffe-Bellany自纽约为时报报道加密货币行业新闻。可以通过电子邮件联系他：davidyb@nytimes.com 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。
items.content: DAVID YAFFE-BELLANY 2026年11月2日 全球最大加密货币交易所币安表示，这起被业内称为史上最大规模加密货币黑客攻击的事件涉及约63亿美元资金。 SeongJoon Cho/Bloomberg At about 4:20 p.m. on Thursday, a string of unusual transactions started to cause alarm at Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange. 周四下午4点20分左右，一连串异常交易开始引起全球最大加密货币交易所币安的警觉。 Money was pouring out of the company’s accounts, a multibillion-dollar deluge of digital coins. It had all the hallmarks of a crypto heist — a high-speed bank robbery conducted over the internet. 资金正从公司的账户中大量流出，价值数十亿美元的数字货币如洪水般倾泻而去。种种迹象都表明，这是一场加密货币盗窃案——一场在互联网上高速进行的银行抢劫。 As the news spread, Binance’s top executives put together an informal war room on Wea, the company’s internal messaging system, with about 100 participants, including specialized cryptocurrency tracers and security personnel. 随着消息传开，币安高管在公司内部通讯系统Wea上临时组建起一个危机应对群组，约有100人参与，其中包括专门追踪加密货币流向的专家和安全人员。 They eventually transitioned to a mass conference call, with 100 boxes on the screen, where employees took turns muting and then unmuting, communicating in a mixture of English and Chinese.
