Westminster）、英国皇家海军和英国皇家空军研究这个课题的约翰·戈尔丁教授（Prof John Golding）说，晕动症通常在八至十岁时最为严重，其后随着接触这类移动环境的经验增加，症状便会减轻。 保持头部不动并打开车窗 随着电动车日益普及，要避开它们可能会愈来愈困难。英国运输部最新数据显示，2026年4月至6月期间，英国新登记的零排放汽车数量较2025年同期上升40.5%。 数据显示，截至2026年6月底，英国道路上所有领有牌照的汽车中，零排放车辆占5.8%。英国计划由2030年起禁止销售全新的纯汽油或纯柴油汽车。 现年24岁、来自伦敦的露辛达·哈里森（Lucinda Harrison）说，她预约的士时，经常到车后才发现那是一辆电动车，之后只好忍受整段旅程中的恶心、冒汗和皮肤湿冷。 她说，一想到要乘坐电动车便感到害怕。最近，一名同事只是顺道载她前往地铁站，短短五分钟的车程，已足以令她感觉“糟透了”。 学者说，乘客可以采取以下几种方法，减轻晕动症。 望向前方车窗，不要看手机或看书。 如果可以，坐在前排乘客座位，不要坐后排。如果必须坐在后排，应选择中间座位，这样仍可看到前方车窗外的景象。 把头靠在头枕上，保持头部不动。 把座椅调低，向后斜躺。 调节呼吸。 打开车窗，让新鲜空气进入车内。 如有需要，可服用晕车药，但这类药物可能引起睡意。 长途旅程开始前，应确保补充足够水分、睡眠充足，并进食不油腻的食物。 专家也说，长时间接触引起晕车的环境，可以令我们逐渐适应。戈尔丁表示，乘坐电动车的次数愈多，身体便愈能适应，也就愈不容易晕车。 Getty Images/Cyndi Monaghan / 望向窗外有助减轻晕动症。儿童和女性作为乘客时，可能较容易出现这种情况。 皇家艺术学院（Royal College of Art）交通设计教授西里尔·迪尔斯（Prof Cyriel Diels）说，汽车制造商也可以采取措施，减轻乘客在电动车上的晕动症。 这些措施包括利用软件令急速加速的过程更加平顺、加入声音系统和细微的座椅震动，提示乘客车辆正在移动，以及提供可调节式再生制动，减少突然减速的情况。 代表英国电动车充电设备制造商的业界组织BEAMA，其代表马特·亚当斯（Matt Adams）说，他相信，“如果未来研究能够找出晕车的原因，汽车制造商便能作出回应，并相应地作出改善”。 但对劳拉来说，她只希望男友尽快把电动车拿去换掉。 她说，那一天愈早到来愈好。 我们使用了人工智慧协助翻译这篇文章，它的原文是英文。在发布之前，BBC记者检查了翻译的内容。 按此了解我们如何使用人工智慧。

items.title: 中國Z世代為何迷上玄學拜佛？ 什麼是「心靈經濟」？
items.description: Getty Images / 中国Z世代为何迷上玄学拜佛？ 什么是“心灵经济”？ 中国年轻人涌向寺庙、算命、塔罗牌和各类灵修产品。这未必是因为他们找到了宗教信仰，而是因为在充满不确定性的时代，他们正试图寻求一丝寄托。 面对就业、收入与未来的焦虑，许多人希望藉此寻求运气、心安以及掌控感。对某些人来说，这意味着去寺庙上香祈福或算命求签；对另一些人来说，则是购买号称能带来好运的手鍊、符咒等各类产品。 商界也敏锐地捕捉到了这一趋势。无论是品牌还是寺庙，都正积极抢滩这个日益蓬勃的“心灵经济”（spiritual economy），将古老传统与现代神秘学转化为针对新一代消费者的商品与体验。 本集Asia Specific节目将一同剖析：这究竟是精神信仰的真正复兴，抑或只是年轻人在面对日益迷茫的未来时，另一种求个心安、分散风险的方式？

items.title: 「工程師治國」：中國為何熱衷於「超級工程」？
items.description: Getty Images / “工程师治国”：中国为何热衷于“超级工程”？ 大型建设工程正在重塑中国——从巨型大坝、庞大的太阳能发电场，到覆盖全国的高铁网络。北京的“工程师思维”能否助其应对气候变化？ 中国的高层领导层长期由工程师主导，国家主席习近平便是其中之一，他曾在1970年代接受过化学工程专业的训练。 从港珠澳大桥到“南水北调”工程，这种对基建的热狂已延伸至能源领域。作为全球最大碳排放国，中国已投入数万亿美元布局风电、核电与特高压输电网。 然而，中国至今仍高度依赖煤电，且大规模工程常破坏在地生态，并造成数百万居民被迫迁徙。那么，北京的这种做法对气候变化意味着什么？

items.title: 機師刀刺同僚企圖劫機 杜拜往以色列航班乘客化解空難
items.description: Reuters 一架从阿联酋杜拜飞往以色列的客机上，在9月30日发生企图空中劫机事件。其中一名机师刺伤另一名副机师后，机上乘客在机人员协助下闯进驾驶舱并合力制伏施袭者，目击画面记录了惊险的瞬间。 涉事客机属于“杜拜航空”（Flydubai），当时正从杜拜飞往以色列，事发后一度失控骤降约1.5万英尺。乘客描述称，涉事机师似乎企图让飞机坠毁。 客机随后发出求救讯号，触发重大安全警报，以色列紧急出动战机拦截该航班。最终，机上其他机制接手操控飞机，紧急降落于沙特阿拉伯，涉嫌施袭的机师被逮捕。 以色列即将举行大选，当局尚未透露涉案副机师的施袭动机。总理内塔尼亚胡表示，目前未能断言事件的背后原因；被福斯新闻问及是否有任何迹象显示伊朗涉事时，他指：“现在下结论仍言之过早。”而以色列国防部长则称此事属于“圣战恐怖主义”行为，但没有提供详细证据。

items.title: 特朗普排除美中合作開發人工智能
items.description: Getty Images / 特朗普在 America.gov 网站的启动仪式上发表讲话。 美国总统特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）表示，不会考虑与中国合资发展人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI；人工智慧），认为这等同于把美国的技术机密交给主要经济竞争对手。 尽管美国民众对人工智能可能带来的风险越加关注，特朗普周二（9月29日）在华盛顿出席一场活动时，再次反对对人工智能发展加设限制，认为这些限制会妨碍这项技术未来的发展。 中国国家主席习近平上周访问白宫后，中美宣布成立新的人工智能对话机制，并计划在11月继续举行会谈。 两国亦设立新的沟通渠道，以避免人工智能相关事件引发误会。 特朗普周二出席利用人工智能，协助简化政府服务的新网站 America.gov 启动活动。特朗普认为美国在人工智慧领域“遥遥领先”，不想与潜在的竞争对手“混为一谈”。 “如果我们这样做，就等于把我们掌握的大量机密交给他们（中国），而他们当然会想得到这些东西，其他国家也会想得到。” 他又说：“坦白说，根本没有第三名⋯⋯现在就是我们和中国之间的竞争。” 特朗普表示，上周与习近平会面时也谈到人工智能，但他仍然反对中美共同发展这项技术。 “这样一来，他们就可以立即接触到一些我们知道、但他们还不知道的东西。”他又说：“我们现在领先中国，也领先其他所有国家，我希望保持这个优势。” 特朗普与习近平会面前，中国外交部曾警告，散播“威胁论”和采取对抗态度都会阻碍人工智能的治理。 Getty Images / 中美AI竞赛：世界变得更危险还是更安全？ 特朗普之后在白宫与政府部门及科技公司代表共进午餐，出席者包括 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Meta 的代表。他说在场人士“普遍认为人工智能应该受到大幅度的自我监管”。 会面后，特朗普向记者表示，与会的科技界领袖已签署一份具有“道德约束力”的文件，希望以此作为防范人工智能潜在危险的“一种保障”。 特朗普又说，政府很可能会在未来数日任命一名“超级智能沙皇”（Super Intelligence Czar）。他周二下午签署行政命令，正式把政府文件中的“人工智能”改称为“超级智能”（Super Intelligence）。 在美国国内，越来越多人担心人工智能可能带来的危险，也有人要求政府加强监管。 Politico 于9月底公布的一项民调显示，每三名美国人就有约两人认为，人工智能至少有“中等程度”的风险，可能最终摧毁人类。 在受访的特朗普支持者中，44%表示，他们宁愿暂停人工智能的发展。 不过，特朗普多次淡化外界对人工智能安全问题的忧虑，形容这些担忧是“骗局”，又把人工智能安全问题与他所称的“全球暖化骗局”相提并论，并声称这是由“激进左翼民主党人”策动的。 人类真的可能被AI灭绝？我们可以如何阻止？ 本文原以英文撰写，我们使用了人工智能协助翻译，并由BBC记者在发布前进行审核。了解更多关于我们如何使用人工智能的资讯。

items.title: 特朗普習近平峰會：沒有說出口的議題可能更重要
items.description: Reuters / 习近平与特朗普在华盛顿的会谈没有发表联合声明，也未取得多少重大突破。 中国星期一（9月28日）公布了更多有关国家主席习近平与唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Tump；川普）上星期会谈中达成共识的资讯，让一些具体成果得以曝光。 但双方没有发表联合声明，也几乎没有重大突破。 相反，两国政府各自发布了这次会晤的说法，这或许显示尽管有白宫参观行程以及加强双边关系的承诺，华盛顿与北京仍对彼此保持戒心。 以下是我们目前已知，以及仍然未知的四件有关此次会谈的事情。 新的人工智能对话与沟通渠道 北京表示，已与华盛顿同意启动新的人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI；人工智慧）对话机制，并安排于11月底进一步会谈。 在两国竞相发展先进人工智能之际，此举显示双方认为有必要为这项日益被应用于商业以至军事规划等领域的技术设立某种防护机制。 双方亦同意建立一条处理人工智能事件的沟通渠道，旨在防止误解或意外事态发展演变成更广泛的对抗。 外界一直密切关注此次会谈是否会在人工智能相关议题上出现任何进展或协议，尤其是在 Anthropic 等美国公司呼吁放慢发展步伐，以及有消息披露 OpenAI 曾未经授权存取澳洲等国家的政府网站，并曾“干预”多个美国政府机构网站之后。 Getty Images / 中美AI竞赛：世界变得更危险还是更安全？ 贸易休战：包括了甚么，又遗漏了甚么 中国官方星期一首次证实，贸易休战已延长至1月10日。 这项短期延长确保两位领导人将于今年稍后在主要国际会议期间再次会面。 特朗普将于11月出席在深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）峰会，而习近平则预定于12月前往迈阿密出席二十国集团（G20）峰会。 世界两大经济体领导人如此频繁会面并不常见。 但北京原本希望休战安排能够延长更久，因此这项为期两个月的延长只能算是温和成果，而非重大突破。 中国确实争取到价值300亿美元（2013亿元人民币；9541亿元新台币）输美商品的较低关税，而北京方面预计也将作出相应幅度的关税下调。 运往美国商店的中国商品，包括玩具、小型家用电器及圣诞装饰品等，都将受惠于较低关税。 特朗普政府亦表示，北京将于2027年及2028年每年至少购买1000万公吨煤炭。 引人注目的是那些未被纳入的内容。 双方没有提及增加中国稀土矿物对美出口，也没有任何迹象显示对美国先进半导体的限制措施将会放宽。 AFP via Getty Images / 运往美国商店的中国玩具将受惠于较低的关税。 美国没有提及台湾，但中国提了 白宫的事实清单并未提及台湾，但这个议题显然是习近平的优先事项。 根据北京方面对会谈的描述，习近平敦促特朗普正式反对台湾独立，并谨慎处理这一问题。 在双方5月上一次会晤后，特朗普透露，习近平曾直接问他，一旦中国发动攻击，美国是否会保卫台湾。 他向记者表示：“只有一个人知道答案，那就是我。”他并提出疑问，美军是否有必要为此“跋涉9500英里（1.53万公里）去打一场战争”。 这一次，特朗普透露的内容少得多。 他在周末向记者表示：“这个问题我们没有谈太多。” 特朗普说：“目前情况很好，一切都在推进之中。他非常了解我的想法。” 这种沉默或许具有重要意义。 特朗普此前曾形容一项拟议中的140亿美元对台军售方案，是他与北京打交道时“非常好的谈判筹码”。这项军售方案已搁置数月。 进一步加深外界困惑的是，美国驻华大使庞德伟（David Perdue）向霍士新闻（Fox News）表示，特朗普曾在峰会期间提出向习近平出售武器。 美国国务院其后澄清，美国法律禁止向中国出售武器，且目前并无此类计划。 北京视这个实行自治的岛屿为中国的一部分。包括美国在内的大多数国家都不承认台湾是一个独立国家，但华盛顿反对任何以武力夺取台湾的企图，并承诺向台湾提供武器。 Anadolu via Getty Images / 台湾问题显然是习近平的首要关切事项。 中国可能正在打开投资大门 中国表示，将允许更多外国金融公司，包括有美国背景的银行、投资公司及保险公司，申请在中国经营业务及设立办事处。但任何批准仍须遵守中国法律法规。 最后这一句是关键。中国正在打开大门，但仍掌控谁可以通过。 外国金融公司长期抱怨，监管障碍、牌照要求以及对出境禁令的忧虑，令它们即使在理论上获准进入市场的情况下，仍难以扩展在华业务。 北京还表示，正讨论增加两国之间航班数量的方法，但双方都未说明将如何实现。 此外，尽管中国已向全球超过75个国家的访客提供免签证入境待遇，但并未将这项安排扩展至美国人。 与此同时，美国国务院仍把赴华旅行列为第二级旅游警示，敦促旅客“提高警觉”，原因包括面临任意执法、出境禁令及拘留的风险。 因此，即使双方都在谈论鼓励商务往来和旅行，一些最大的障碍仍然牢牢存在。 BBC / 中国、台湾民众如何看“习特会”？专家如何解读峰会成果？ 那么，我们其实都知道些甚么？ 这次峰会带来了更多对话，但目前几乎没有改变任何重大决策。从先进科技到台湾等最具争议性的议题，仍然未获解决。 但对两位领导人而言，这是熟悉的结果：承诺建立更多沟通渠道、作出有限的经济让步，以及提出温和的稳定双边关系方案。 而尽管双方都仍致力维持稳定关系，持续的美中对话似乎远比要求任何一个超级大国作出妥协来得容易。 本文原以英文撰写，我们使用了人工智能协助翻译，并由BBC记者在发布前进行审核。了解更多关于我们如何使用人工智能的资讯。

items.title: 為何特朗普在國宴上送習近平一座華麗的白頭海鵰雕像？
items.description: EPA / 特朗普称，他与第一夫人梅拉尼娅一同参与了雕像的设计。 美国总统特朗普在华盛顿一场盛大的国宴上，向中国国家主席习近平赠送了一座白头海鵰雕像。这种鸟类原生于北美，也是美国的国家象征。 这份礼物在星期四的国宴上，于一众贵宾面前亮相。特朗普说，它体现了“美国自由翱翔的精神”。 他表示，自己和第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普都有参与雕像的设计。 这座雕像亦反映了国际外交中一个珍贵但有时相当棘手的环节：送礼。 此类礼物虽只是小小心意，却别具意义，也呼应习近平与特朗普三天峰会的一项更宏大目标——在两个全球超级大国的领导人之间建立私人情谊。 美商亚洲集团（The Asia Group）合夥人康达（Daniel Kritenbrink）说：“他们要讨论所有这些复杂的问题，但说到底，他们仍然是两个人。” 他说：“所以，这种私人关系是有意义的。我认为交换礼物是其中一个重要部分。” 康达曾任美国外交官超过30年，大部分时间在亚洲工作。他说，对习近平而言，私人关系尤其重要。 他认为，特朗普与习近平之间直接建立的关系，是维系“全球最复杂、影响最深远的双边关系”的黏合剂。 康达形容这种“领袖层级外交”，他认为特朗普同样重视。 送礼在特朗普的总统任期内一直占有独特的位置。 这位美国总统曾经收到豪华大型客机、刻字金条、镶满钻石和宝石的金戒指等礼物。 挪威国际事务研究所（Norwegian Institute of International Affairs）的奥勒·雅各布·森丁（Ole Jacob Sending）说：“如果从这个角度理解特朗普的总统任期，我认为广义而言，送礼确实是他行事方式的一部分。” 星期四早上，习近平宣布向亚特兰大一间动物园赠送两只中国大熊猫，同时推出一项新的学生交流计划，未来五年将接待10万名美国学生到中国留学。 习近平说：“大熊猫一直是中美人民友谊的使者。几天后，两只大熊猫‘平平’和‘福双’将来到亚特兰大动物园的新家，与美国人民见面。” 目前尚不清楚习近平是否还赠送了其他礼物。BBC已就此联络白宫。 如今，赠送豪华礼物的外交传统，主要仍见于海湾国家和威权政府。 莫滕·斯库姆斯鲁德·安德森（Morten Skumsrud Anderson）曾与森丁共同研究外交与送礼文化。他说：“中国等威权国家会赠送昂贵得多的礼物。” 安德森说，在西方，这项传统已受到民主制度的制衡和限制，重要性因而有所降低。 例如，美国宪法中的“薪酬条款”限制总统可以从外国政府收取的礼物价值。 目前上限是525美元（397英镑）。如果礼物价值高于这个金额，便会成为联邦政府财产，除非总统选择自掏腰包将它买下。 同样，美国总统如果要送出价值超过特定金额的礼物，一般也要经过国会程序，除非由总统本人付款。 森丁说：“这里涉及大量规则和礼宾程序。要仔细考虑送甚么礼物、在哪里交换礼物、以甚么方式进行，以及甚么时候进行。” 他说：“所有这些事情都是经过高度编排的，而且较低层级的人员会提前几个星期反复磋商。” 安德森补充：“这可不是在机场临时买的礼物。” 2013年习近平对美国进行国事访问期间，时任总统奥巴马送给他一张刻有文字的长椅，以加州原生的红杉木制成。两人当时正是在加州会面，之后更一同坐在长椅上，微笑让传媒拍照。 相比之下，2009年的一次礼物交换就没有那么成功。 当时英国首相戈登·布朗（Gordon Brown）送给奥巴马一个装饰用的书桌笔座，以一艘历史悠久的反奴隶贸易船只木材制成；奥巴马回赠戈登·布朗的则是一套DVD，据报却无法在英国的DVD播放器上播放。 森丁说：“这算是一次颇尴尬的礼物交换。” 幸好，戈登·布朗和奥巴马是盟友领导人，而不是要设法解决看似难以化解分歧的深层竞争对手。 森丁说：“你可不想把事情搞砸。”他补充，一份不恰当的礼物，甚至有可能破坏更大的外交目标。 而在特朗普与习近平这次会面中，潜在利害尤其重大。 这是特朗普第二个总统任期开始以来，两人第三次面对面会晤。两国正竞逐迅速发展的人工智能产业主导地位，而外界对人工智能可能带来末日式灾难的忧虑也日益增加。 此次峰会亦是在一场激烈的中美贸易战之后举行。双方目前只是以临时休战暂时化解争端，并在这次访问期间延长休战期限。 所以，康达说，那就安排军机飞越上空、准备表演、把酒杯斟满，再交换礼物吧。 他说：“礼宾、场面和交换礼物，全部都只是达成一个目标的手段，那就是维持稳定的美中关系。” “无论哪一天，要我在脆弱的休战和白热化的贸易战之间选，我都会选前者。” 本文原以英文撰写，我们使用了人工智能协助翻译，并由BBC记者在发布前进行审核。了解更多关于我们如何使用人工智能的资讯。

items.title: 從年輕縣官到國家主席：習近平41年來的訪美影像
items.description: Reuters 1985年，31岁的习近平以中共河北省正定县委书记身份首次访问美国，行程包括三藩市和艾奥瓦州。当时，他此行主要是考察农业和地方发展。 四十多年来，习近平先后以地方官员、中国国家副主席和国家主席等不同身份访美。随着职位转变，访问内容也由地方交流和经贸考察，逐步转为中美元首会晤和多边外交活动。 本周三至五（9月23日至25日）将是习近平第11次官式访问美国。过去的访问横跨中美关系多个阶段，既有地方层面的交流，也有在白宫、庄园和国际峰会上的高层会晤。 BBC中文透过历年照片，回顾习近平四十多年来的访美经历，以及不同时期行程和角色的变化。 县官出国——1985年 根据中国官方媒体纪录，习近平第一次踏足美国，是作为中共河北省正定县委书记，时为1985年4月，中共政权与华盛顿建交刚满六年之际。 习近平当时31岁，代表团连他在内共有五人：河北省束鹿县县长白润璋、石家庄地区外事办公室秘书夏文义、石家庄地区科学技术委员会副主任刘录清，和石家庄地区经济委员会主任于锡庆。 Xinhua/Alamy / 旧金山（三藩市）是习近平一行的第一站，他在地标金门大桥前拍下了这张照片。 但这次行程的重点是到访有“美国粮仓”之称的艾奥瓦州（Iowa；爱荷华／衣阿华），习近平一行在小镇马斯卡廷（Muscatine）考察农业和畜牧业。 据接待单位艾奥瓦州姊妹省州委员会（Iowa Sister States）纪录，习近平一行在美国逗留了15天。 Muscatine Journal/Quad-City Times/ZUMA Wire/Alamy / 习近平（后右二）到访马斯卡廷镇的两天里，由当地人萨拉·兰蒂（Sarah Lande；前右二）等接待。兰蒂当时是艾奥瓦州姊妹省州委员会的创始执行主任。夏文义（前左一）担任中方翻译。CCTV / 习近平一行到访，当时成为了马斯卡廷的大新闻。CCTV / 在2023年一次演说中，习近平回忆道：“这是我同美国民众首次面对面接触⋯⋯对我来说，他们就是美国。”CCTV / 曾参与接待的卢卡·贝隆（Luca Berrone）对中国官方新华社回忆说，当时的习近平“总带着笑容，很有礼貌，遇到的每个人都很喜欢他”。The Washington Post via Getty Images / 习近平当时被安排在马斯卡廷居民德沃切克夫妇（Eleanor and Thomas Dvorchak）家中留宿，这座民宅2013年被艾奥瓦州华商程利军（Glad Cheng）购入，改建成中美友谊屋展览馆。Xinhua/Alamy / 德沃切克夫妇当时让习近平在儿子格利（Gary Dvorchak，图）的睡房留宿了两个晚上。据报导，这是因为格利当时在外地上大学，房间正好空着。 自马斯卡廷之旅后，习近平于1992年、1993年和2006年三度访美，前两次身份是中共福建福州市委书记，最后一次是浙江省委书记。 国家级回访——2012年 2008年，习近平升任中国国家副主席，晋身国家领导人。2012年，他首次以这个身份官式访美，来了个“回到原点”。 AFP via Getty Images / 中国国家副主席要来马斯卡廷，镇上的麦当劳在电子广告牌上写道“欢迎回来”。Iowa Governor's Office via Getty Images / 这次习近平来到萨拉·兰蒂的家作客。当时的报导说，有迹象表明，1985年那次访问给习近平留下了良好的印象。此次访美行程紧张，他仍坚持故地重访。AFP via Getty Images / 不同阵营的集会者也随之而来。亲西藏（左）与亲北京（右）团体隔着马路，一边是示威，一边是助威。 习近平此次行程历时五天，从首都华盛顿，到艾奥瓦马斯卡廷，再到加州洛杉矶。 Getty Images / 探访马斯卡廷前，习近平到白宫会晤时任美国副总统乔·拜登（Joe Biden，右），两人在镜头面前笑容满面。当天正好是情人节。Reuters / 时任总统奥巴马也在椭圆形办公室内接见了习近平。Getty Images / 习近平在洛杉矶看了一场NBA篮球赛，由洛杉矶湖人对凤凰城太阳。 庄园会晤登场——2013年 2013年6月7日至8日，习近平第六次访美，行程包括与时任总统奥巴马（Barack Obama；欧巴马）在加州安纳伯格庄园（Annenberg Retreat at Sunnylands）进行“庄园会晤”。 这一年60岁的习近平，刚接任了国家主席一职。这次是习近平与奥巴马第二次在美国会晤，但作为两国元首会晤，则是第一次。 Reuters / “庄园会晤”被定性为非正式会晤，双方脱下了领带。Reuters / 不止两位国家元首，就连随后的大范围会谈，两国官员也统一不打领带。AFP via Getty Images / “庄园会晤”被形容为两人认识对方、建立关系的机会。双方形容会面独特、正面和有建设性。 亮相联合国——2015年 时隔两年，习近平再次踏上美国土地，而这次是正式的国事访问。 习近平整个美国行程历时七天。其中9月22日至25日是对美国的国事访问，随后三天则转往纽约联合国总部，出席联合国成立70周年系列活动。 中国社交媒体上当时出现了责难外交部的声音，因习近平访美行程与时任罗马天主教教宗方济各（Pope Francis）的访美行程重叠，习近平似乎被教宗“抢了风头”。 但与此同时，两位领袖同处美国，曾引起观察人士憧憬中梵元首能趁机会晤“破冰”，而这最终并未发生。 翌年，习近平再到华盛顿，出席第四届核安全峰会。 Reuters / 习近平此行首站是西岸航空工业重镇西雅图，他参观了波音公司的飞机生产线。Reuters / 奥巴马与习近平再次以休闲商务装示人——奥巴马安排在白宫对面的布莱尔宫（Blair House）以私宴款待习近平。Getty Images / 美方翌日再举行国宴，欢迎中方一行。Reuters / 习近平最后一段行程是到联合国大会发言。这是他就任中国国家主席至今唯一一次亲自到纽约市出席联大会议。 初会特朗普——2017年 2017年1月，特朗普首次就任美国总统。4月，习近平访美24小时，到佛罗里达州的特朗普私人俱乐部海湖庄园（Mar-a-Lago estate）会晤对方。 在这场峰会进行途中，特朗普下令空袭叙利亚。如此时机，引起了广泛讨论。 Reuters / 与习近平首次碰面后，特朗普反复强调他与中国元首关系“非常好”——尽管之后爆发了中美贸易战。 疫情后的“习拜会”——2023年 新冠病毒病疫情（COVID-19 pandemic）下，习近平自2020年起暂停外访活动将近三年。 2023年11月，习近平到三藩市（旧金山）出席亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会，期间与“升任”了美国总统的“老熟人”拜登。 这也是习近平在2026年之前，最后一次到访美国。 Reuters / 习近平与拜登在这次峰会上达成恢复军事高层对话等共识，但一年后特朗普再次当选总统，中美关系再迎变数。2023年：“习拜会”后，中美同意恢复军事对话、领导通话。
items.content: Reuters 1985年，31岁的习近平以中共河北省正定县委书记身份首次访问美国，行程包括三藩市和艾奥瓦州。当时，他此行主要是考察农业和地方发展。 四十多年来，习近平先后以地方官员、中国国家副主席和国家主席等不同身份访美。随着职位转变，访问内容也由地方交流和经贸考察，逐步转为中美元首会晤和多边外交活动。 本周三至五（9月23日至25日）将是习近平第11次官式访问美国。过去的访问横跨中美关系多个阶段，既有地方层面的交流，也有在白宫、庄园和国际峰会上的高层会晤。 BBC中文透过历年照片，回顾习近平四十多年来的访美经历，以及不同时期行程和角色的变化。 县官出国——1985年 根据中国官方媒体纪录，习近平第一次踏足美国，是作为中共河北省正定县委书记，时为1985年4月，中共政权与华盛顿建交刚满六年之际。 习近平当时31岁，代表团连他在内共有五人：河北省束鹿县县长白润璋、石家庄地区外事办公室秘书夏文义、石家庄地区科学技术委员会副主任刘录清，和石家庄地区经济委员会主任于锡庆。 Xinhua/Alamy / 旧金山（三藩市）是习近平一行的第一站，他在地标金门大桥前拍下了这张照片。 但这次行程的重点是到访有“美国粮仓”之称的艾奥瓦州（Iowa；爱荷华／衣阿华），习近平一行在小镇马斯卡廷（Muscatine）考察农业和畜牧业。 据接待单位艾奥瓦州姊妹省州委员会（Iowa Sister States）纪录，习近平一行在美国逗留了15天。 Muscatine Journal/Quad-City Times/ZUMA Wire/Alamy / 习近平（后右二）到访马斯卡廷镇的两天里，由当地人萨拉·兰蒂（Sarah Lande；前右二）等接待。兰蒂当时是艾奥瓦州姊妹省州委员会的创始执行主任。夏文义（前左一）担任中方翻译。 CCTV / 习近平一行到访，当时成为了马斯卡廷的大新闻。 CCTV / 在2023年一次演说中，习近平回忆道：“这是我同美国民众首次面对面接触⋯⋯对我来说，他们就是美国。” CCTV / 曾参与接待的卢卡·贝隆（Luca Berrone）对中国官方新华社回忆说，当时的习近平“总带着笑容，很有礼貌，遇到的每个人都很喜欢他”。 The Washington Post via Getty Images / 习近平当时被安排在马斯卡廷居民德沃切克夫妇（Eleanor and Thomas Dvorchak）家中留宿，这座民宅2013年被艾奥瓦州华商程利军（Glad Cheng）购入，改建成中美友谊屋展览馆。 Xinhua/Alamy / 德沃切克夫妇当时让习近平在儿子格利（Gary Dvorchak，图）的睡房留宿了两个晚上。据报导，这是因为格利当时在外地上大学，房间正好空着。 自马斯卡廷之旅后，习近平于1992年、1993年和2006年三度访美，前两次身份是中共福建福州市委书记，最后一次是浙江省委书记。 国家级回访——2012年 2008年，习近平升任中国国家副主席，晋身国家领导人。2012年，他首次以这个身份官式访美，来了个“回到原点”。 AFP via Getty Images / 中国国家副主席要来马斯卡廷，镇上的麦当劳在电子广告牌上写道“欢迎回来”。 Iowa Governor's Office via Getty Images / 这次习近平来到萨拉·兰蒂的家作客。当时的报导说，有迹象表明，1985年那次访问给习近平留下了良好的印象。此次访美行程紧张，他仍坚持故地重访。 AFP via Getty Images / 不同阵营的集会者也随之而来。亲西藏（左）与亲北京（右）团体隔着马路，一边是示威，一边是助威。 习近平此次行程历时五天，从首都华盛顿，到艾奥瓦马斯卡廷，再到加州洛杉矶。 Getty Images / 探访马斯卡廷前，习近平到白宫会晤时任美国副总统乔·拜登（Joe Biden，右），两人在镜头面前笑容满面。当天正好是情人节。 Reuters / 时任总统奥巴马也在椭圆形办公室内接见了习近平。 Getty Images / 习近平在洛杉矶看了一场NBA篮球赛，由洛杉矶湖人对凤凰城太阳。 庄园会晤登场——2013年 2013年6月7日至8日，习近平第六次访美，行程包括与时任总统奥巴马（Barack Obama；欧巴马）在加州安纳伯格庄园（Annenberg Retreat at Sunnylands）进行“庄园会晤”。 这一年60岁的习近平，刚接任了国家主席一职。这次是习近平与奥巴马第二次在美国会晤，但作为两国元首会晤，则是第一次。 Reuters / “庄园会晤”被定性为非正式会晤，双方脱下了领带。 Reuters / 不止两位国家元首，就连随后的大范围会谈，两国官员也统一不打领带。 AFP via Getty Images / “庄园会晤”被形容为两人认识对方、建立关系的机会。双方形容会面独特、正面和有建设性。 亮相联合国——2015年 时隔两年，习近平再次踏上美国土地，而这次是正式的国事访问。 习近平整个美国行程历时七天。其中9月22日至25日是对美国的国事访问，随后三天则转往纽约联合国总部，出席联合国成立70周年系列活动。 items.title: 2026台灣地方選舉：「九合一」為何重要？選舉時程是什麼？
items.description: Getty Images / 台湾的地方选举又称“九合一”选举，图为2022年选举开票。 台湾将在今年11月28日举行“九合一”地方选举，选出直辖市长和县市长在内9类地方公职。 其中，蓝绿差距较小、全台人口最多的新北市，被视为决定胜负的重要战场。 分析指出，这场选举不仅是针对总统赖清德的执政信任票，亦是2028年总统大选的起跑赛。对于两岸路线遭党内质疑的国民党主席郑丽文而言，此役也是她能否取得总统大选提名的关键。 相较于“抗中保台”，此次选举议题更聚焦于民生经济。选前三个月，赖清德宣布派发一万现金、在野阵营则提出三项公投提案，都被外界认为是选举前的政治攻防的一环。 Getty Images / 九合一选举被视为对总统赖清德的执政信任票，图为赖清德在2024年双十发表讲话。 2028总统大选前哨战 台湾的地方选举又称“九合一”选举，历届选举多数落在总统任期中段的年底，故被视为总统的“期中考”。 对身兼民进党主席的赖清德而言，他不仅须扛起选举成败的责任，力求2028连任的他，也需维持气势，稳固党内共主的地位。而对国民党主席郑丽文来说，假如她希望参选2028，这也会是她显示领导力的重要一役。 台湾东海大学政治系教授张峻豪对BBC中文分析，在国会朝野对峙不断的背景下，民进党若能守住甚至扩大地方版图，等于替少数执政增添一定程度的正当性；反之，就可能被迫在国会调整路线。 他续指，国民党的压力则落在郑丽文身上，这是她接任党主席后的第一次全面检验，党内对其两岸主张本有分歧，一旦败选，她的路线很可能被拿出来检讨，内部对抗性也会随之升高。 民众党方面，张峻豪认为，这次能在地方拿下多少议员席次、斩获多少中间选民选票，关系到它往后的生存策略。在“蓝白合”的情况下，如果无法展现地方实力，民众党的空间恐被国民党挤压。 “蓝白下一阶段要不要合、又要怎么合，都会被这次的结果牵动。” Getty Images / 图为2022年九合一地方选举开票 从“九合一”看党派势力消长 “九合一”的意思，是把九类地方选举合并于同一天投票，选出县市长、市议员、乡长、里长等。有关安排自2014年起沿用至今，选举每四年一次。 此次选举约有1965万名选民，当中60万人为“首投族”。中央选举委员会表示，地方选举加上公投，预计需动员30万名选务工作人员。 外界将焦点放在层级最高的地方首长竞选，共计22席的直辖市长、县（市）长选举，以此判别执政民进党与在野国民党及民众党的势力消长。 上一届2022年地方选举中，在野蓝白阵营夺得13个县市的首长席次，而执政绿营只有5个。当时选举显现了国民党坚强的基层实力，时任民众党籍的高虹安选上新竹市长，奠定了第三大党的民意基础。而民进党的挫败，也显现其地方经营能力的衰弱。 此次2026年选举中，绿营试图在新北、嘉义、彰化、宜兰等县市翻盘，蓝营除了守城外，也试图插旗南部的高雄市。 BBC 新北市成焦点 这次选举中，新北市被视为决定成败的重要战役。 绿营候选人为现任立法委员苏巧慧，在野阵营则在民众党主席黄国昌礼让下，由国民党推派前行政院秘书长李四川参选。 纵使现任国民党籍市长侯友宜在2022年选举中以62%的得票率高票当选，但以目前民调来看，新北市民的蓝绿支持度已回档到五五波，其中关键变数为数量庞大的中间选民。 在2026年4月的美丽岛民调，新北市民支持民进党及泛绿的比例约34.4%；而支持国民党、民众党及泛蓝的比例约31.6%，多达27.1%的选民表示自己是“中立或看党不看人”。 另一份由新台湾国策智库调查的民调结果相仿，有26.5%受访的新北市民政党倾向是“不偏任何党”或“未表态”。 “因为中间选民每次投票都可能投不同政党、甚至不去投票，所以候选人有没有比较吸睛的政见或者让人喜欢的特质是很重要的，”国立台北大学公共行政暨政策学系教授刘嘉薇向BBC中文说。 她表示，目前两位候选人在主要政见上还没有很突出，所以目前选情走向仍有很大的不确定性。 外界观察“蓝白合” “蓝白合”的成败也是此次选举外界观察重点之一。 在主要县市首长选举上，蓝白在新竹市与嘉义县共同支持无党籍候选人；白营则在蓝营礼让下仅在嘉义市提名张启楷，并在其余县市支持国民党候选人。 然而，在更加地方层级的选战上，蓝白却出现了分裂的状况。在新竹县竹北市的市长选举中，蓝白就在谈判破局后各自推派了自己的候选人，引发争议。 学者张峻豪向BBC中文表示，随着民众党在地方支持度下滑，国民党对蓝白合的态度似乎也有所改变。 “蓝白要合，当然也就是因为白有相当程度的支持度。如果在某些地区，蓝营本身就可以去囊括选票的情况下，为何蓝营需要蓝白合？”他强调，国民党对蓝白合的真正盘算是在2028总统大选，而非此次地方选举。 此外，地方选举也让三大党外的其他小党有参与议员与村里长等基层公职选举的空间。去年底，时代力量、小民参政欧巴桑联盟、台湾基进与台湾绿党合作成立“台湾前进阵线”，一同推派35位候选人参选议员及乡镇市民代表，挑战民众党的第三势力共主地位。 然而，张峻豪也提醒，所谓第三势力的选民投票意愿有多高，仍是一大问题。 “随着民众党整体支持度下滑，我在地方上听到的是反蓝绿的中间选民对于政治已经越来越冷感了，他们现在整体政治参与度都在下降。到了选举时，他们会愿意出来投票吗？” AFP 公投再次绑定大选 与本届九合一选举同日举办的，还有“废除非核家园”的公投议题。这是台湾自2018年来，第四次与核能相关的公投案。 有鉴于2018年地方选举时，10件公投案绑定大选举办导致选务混乱，出现了边投票边开票的情况，民进党政府在2019年修法，将公投案与主要选举年错开，引来在野的国民党批评。 凭藉国会多数，国民党、民众党提案再次将公投绑定回大选。新版《公投法》于2025年底三读通过。 学者刘嘉薇向BBC中文表示，公投若与大选分开举办，容易导致选民疲劳，使投票率下降。 “我认为公投跟大选绑在一起对公共政策的讨论比较有帮助。这样有助于提升投票率，候选人也能藉机论述。”她说。

台湾东海大学政治系教授张峻豪对BBC中文分析，在国会朝野对峙不断的背景下，民进党若能守住甚至扩大地方版图，等于替少数执政增添一定程度的正当性；反之，就可能被迫在国会调整路线。 他续指，国民党的压力则落在郑丽文身上，这是她接任党主席后的第一次全面检验，党内对其两岸主张本有分歧，一旦败选，她的路线很可能被拿出来检讨，内部对抗性也会随之升高。 民众党方面，张峻豪认为，这次能在地方拿下多少议员席次、斩获多少中间选民选票，关系到它往后的生存策略。在“蓝白合”的情况下，如果无法展现地方实力，民众党的空间恐被国民党挤压。 “蓝白下一阶段要不要合、又要怎么合，都会被这次的结果牵动。” Getty Images / 图为2022年九合一地方选举开票 从“九合一”看党派势力消长 “九合一”的意思，是把九类地方选举合并于同一天投票，选出县市长、市议员、乡长、里长等。有关安排自2014年起沿用至今，选举每四年一次。 此次选举约有1965万名选民，当中60万人为“首投族”。中央选举委员会表示，地方选举加上公投，预计需动员30万名选务工作人员。 外界将焦点放在层级最高的地方首长竞选，共计22席的直辖市长、县（市）长选举，以此判别执政民进党与在野国民党及民众党的势力消长。 上一届2022年地方选举中，在野蓝白阵营夺得13个县市的首长席次，而执政绿营只有5个。当时选举显现了国民党坚强的基层实力，时任民众党籍的高虹安选上新竹市长，奠定了第三大党的民意基础。而民进党的挫败，也显现其地方经营能力的衰弱。 此次2026年选举中，绿营试图在新北、嘉义、彰化、宜兰等县市翻盘，蓝营除了守城外，也试图插旗南部的高雄市。 BBC 新北市成焦点 这次选举中，新北市被视为决定成败的重要战役。 绿营候选人为现任立法委员苏巧慧，在野阵营则在民众党主席黄国昌礼让下，由国民党推派前行政院秘书长李四川参选。 纵使现任国民党籍市长侯友宜在2022年选举中以62%的得票率高票当选，但以目前民调来看，新北市民的蓝绿支持度已回档到五五波，其中关键变数为数量庞大的中间选民。 在2026年4月的美丽岛民调，新北市民支持民进党及泛绿的比例约34.4%；而支持国民党、民众党及泛蓝的比例约31.6%，多达27.1%的选民表示自己是“中立或看党不看人”。 另一份由新台湾国策智库调查的民调结果相仿，有26.5%受访的新北市民政党倾向是“不偏任何党”或“未表态”。 “因为中间选民每次投票都可能投不同政党、甚至不去投票，所以候选人有没有比较吸睛的政见或者让人喜欢的特质是很重要的，”国立台北大学公共行政暨政策学系教授刘嘉薇向BBC中文说。 她表示，目前两位候选人在主要政见上还没有很突出，所以目前选情走向仍有很大的不确定性。 外界观察“蓝白合” “蓝白合”的成败也是此次选举外界观察重点之一。 在主要县市首长选举上，蓝白在新竹市与嘉义县共同支持无党籍候选人；白营则在蓝营礼让下仅在嘉义市提名张启楷，并在其余县市支持国民党候选人。 然而，在更加地方层级的选战上，蓝白却出现了分裂的状况。在新竹县竹北市的市长选举中，蓝白就在谈判破局后各自推派了自己的候选人，引发争议。 学者张峻豪向BBC中文表示，随着民众党在地方支持度下滑，国民党对蓝白合的态度似乎也有所改变。 “蓝白要合，当然也就是因为白有相当程度的支持度。如果在某些地区，蓝营本身就可以去囊括选票的情况下，为何蓝营需要蓝白合？”他强调，国民党对蓝白合的真正盘算是在2028总统大选，而非此次地方选举。 此外，地方选举也让三大党外的其他小党有参与议员与村里长等基层公职选举的空间。去年底，时代力量、小民参政欧巴桑联盟、台湾基进与台湾绿党合作成立“台湾前进阵线”，一同推派35位候选人参选议员及乡镇市民代表，挑战民众党的第三势力共主地位。 然而，张峻豪也提醒，所谓第三势力的选民投票意愿有多高，仍是一大问题。 “随着民众党整体支持度下滑，我在地方上听到的是反蓝绿的中间选民对于政治已经越来越冷感了，他们现在整体政治参与度都在下降。到了选举时，他们会愿意出来投票吗？” AFP 公投再次绑定大选 与本届九合一选举同日举办的，还有“废除非核家园”的公投议题。这是台湾自2018年来，第四次与核能相关的公投案。 有鉴于2018年地方选举时，10件公投案绑定大选举办导致选务混乱，出现了边投票边开票的情况，民进党政府在2019年修法，将公投案与主要选举年错开，引来在野的国民党批评。 凭藉国会多数，国民党、民众党提案再次将公投绑定回大选。新版《公投法》于2025年底三读通过。 学者刘嘉薇向BBC中文表示，公投若与大选分开举办，容易导致选民疲劳，使投票率下降。 “我认为公投跟大选绑在一起对公共政策的讨论比较有帮助。这样有助于提升投票率，候选人也能藉机论述。”她说。

items.title: pbakaus/impeccable
items.description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships. https://impeccable.style Impeccable The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, and catch AI slop before it ships. From your project root: npx impeccable install Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ($impeccable init on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs. Without Impeccable With Impeccable Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water. For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study: a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page. Why Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects. Words for what you want. "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. /impeccable bolder the pricing cards loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target. A reviewer. critique scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. audit checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish). A slop detector. 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key. Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component: /impeccable critique the pricing cards How it works Run /impeccable init once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes PRODUCT.md. Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md, so changes stay on-brand. More on context files. Then name a command and a target: /impeccable critique the onboarding flow /impeccable quieter the landing page /impeccable polish settings /impeccable harden checkout Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut. 24 commands Commands Steer bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects Review critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report Finish polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states Iterate live live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking Plan and set up shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system The 24th, craft, is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs. On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command. Live mode /impeccable live opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. Iterate in the browser. Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your package.json's optional impeccable:manual-edit-validate script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo. Three ways to run the detector In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks. In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent: npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge) npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173. Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font". To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores. In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay. Installation npx impeccable install The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global. Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness. Node is only needed for npx. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/. Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable, then open /plugin and install Impeccable. GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details. Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook. Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor Commit .gitmodules, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive. To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable, rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force. Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style, or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. Tool Repo folder Global skills folder Claude Code .claude/ ~/.claude/skills/ Cursor .cursor/ Codex CLI, Replit Agent .agents/ ~/.agents/skills/ Devin .devin/ ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/ GitHub Copilot .github/ Gemini CLI .gemini/ Google Antigravity .agent/ ~/.gemini/config/skills/ OpenCode .opencode/ Grok Build .grok/ ~/.grok/skills/ Hermes Agent .hermes/ ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/ DeepSeek Harness .dsh/ ${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/ Pi .pi/ Qoder .qoder/ ~/.qoder/skills/ Rovo Dev .rovodev/ ~/.rovodev/skills/ Mistral Vibe .vibe/ ~/.vibe/skills/ Trae .trae/ ~/.trae/skills/ Trae China .trae-cn/ ~/.trae-cn/skills/ For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/. Notes: A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path. OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable. Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step. Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs. Restart Trae after copying. impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory. Project files and git Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/. A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json, live/config.json, design.json, surfaces/*.md, and critique/*.md. Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state. Copy the .gitignore entries # impeccable-ignore-start # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides. # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace. # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json, # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md. **/.impeccable/config.local.json **/.impeccable/hook.cache.json **/.impeccable/hook.pending.json **/.impeccable/*.png **/.impeccable/review/ **/.impeccable/questions/ **/.impeccable/live/server.json **/.impeccable/live/sessions/ **/.impeccable/live/previews/ **/.impeccable/live/annotations/ **/.impeccable/live/cache/ **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-apply-transaction.json **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-events.jsonl **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-evidence/ **/.impeccable/live/pending-manual-edits.json **/.impeccable/live/deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json **/.impeccable/live/*.png # impeccable-ignore-end The folders that hold decision-round state (.impeccable/questions/, .impeccable/mocks/worlds/) also ignore themselves. A .gitignore can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run git rm --cached . Good to know Build path. For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. init asks once and saves the answer as buildPath in .impeccable/config.json; the decision page lets you override it for one session. The choice only appears when your harness can generate images. Image generation · Configuration. Hooks run outside model approval. In Claude Code, installed command hooks run even when you deny the model's own commands, so the first edit can download the engine. Review installed hooks before unattended runs, or pass --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}' to turn them off for a run. The installer leaves hook entries it didn't add alone. Something broken? /impeccable doctor finds stale context files, unused settings, and broken hooks. Fix setup problems. Telemetry. When a new design starts, the skill fetches a set of visual directions from the impeccable.style catalog. Turning telemetry off doesn't stop that request; it stops the anonymous record of which directions were shown and which one you picked, which is how the catalog learns what works. Your project name, files, code, and PRODUCT.md are never sent. Disable telemetry with npx impeccable telemetry off, DO_NOT_TRACK=1, or "telemetry": false in .impeccable/config.json for the whole project. The full list of what is sent is on the privacy page. Community Issues for bugs, questions, and ideas. Outside contributions start with an issue; see DEVELOP.md. Changelog for what shipped. Follow @pbakaus for release notes and new rules. License Apache 2.0. See LICENSE. Impeccable started from Anthropic's frontend-design skill. Created by Paul Bakaus

To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc --> . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores . In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay . Installation npx impeccable install The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global . Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust . In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness . Node is only needed for npx . The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/ . Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable , then open /plugin and install Impeccable. GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable . Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details . Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook. Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor Commit .gitmodules , the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive . To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable , rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force . Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style , or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. Tool Repo folder Global skills folder Claude Code .claude/ ~/.claude/skills/ Cursor .cursor/ Codex CLI, Replit Agent .agents/ ~/.agents/skills/ Devin .devin/ ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/ GitHub Copilot .github/ Gemini CLI .gemini/ Google Antigravity .agent/ ~/.gemini/config/skills/ OpenCode .opencode/ Grok Build .grok/ ~/.grok/skills/ Hermes Agent .hermes/ ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/ DeepSeek Harness .dsh/ ${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/ Pi .pi/ Qoder .qoder/ ~/.qoder/skills/ Rovo Dev .rovodev/ ~/.rovodev/skills/ Mistral Vibe .vibe/ ~/.vibe/skills/ Trae .trae/ ~/.trae/skills/ Trae China .trae-cn/ ~/.trae-cn/skills/ For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/ . Notes: A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path. OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable . Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step. Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs. Restart Trae after copying. impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory. Project files and git Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/ . A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json , live/config.json , design.json , surfaces/*.md , and critique/*.md . Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state. Copy the .gitignore entries # impeccable-ignore-start # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides. # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace. # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json, # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md. **/.impeccable/config.local.json **/.impeccable/hook.cache.json **/.impeccable/hook.pending.json **/.impeccable/*.png **/.impeccable/review/ **/.impeccable/questions/ **/.impeccable/live/server.json **/.impeccable/live/sessions/ **/.impeccable/live/previews/ **/.impeccable/live/annotations/ **/.impeccable/live/cache/ **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-apply-transaction.json **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-events.jsonl **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-evidence/ **/.impeccable/live/pending-manual-edits.json **/.impeccable/live/deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json **/.impeccable/live/*.png # impeccable-ignore-end The folders that hold decision-round state ( .impeccable/questions/ , .impeccable/mocks/worlds/ ) also ignore themselves. A .gitignore can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run git rm --cached <path> . Good to know Build path. For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. init asks once and saves the answer as buildPath in .impeccable/config.json ; the decision page lets you override it for one session. The choice only appears when your harness can generate images. Image generation · Configuration . Hooks run outside model approval. In Claude Code, installed command hooks run even when you deny the model's own commands, so the first edit can download the engine. Review installed hooks before unattended runs, or pass --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}' to turn them off for a run. The installer leaves hook entries it didn't add alone. Something broken? /impeccable doctor finds stale context files, unused settings, and broken hooks. Fix setup problems . Telemetry. When a new design starts, the skill fetches a set of visual directions from the impeccable.style catalog. Turning telemetry off doesn't stop that request; it stops the anonymous record of which directions were shown and which one you picked, which is how the catalog learns what works. Your project name, files, code, and PRODUCT.md are never sent. Disable telemetry with npx impeccable telemetry off , DO_NOT_TRACK=1 , or "telemetry": false in .impeccable/config.json for the whole project. The full list of what is sent is on the privacy page . Community Issues for bugs, questions, and ideas. Outside contributions start with an issue; see DEVELOP.md . Changelog for what shipped. Follow @pbakaus for release notes and new rules. License Apache 2.0. See LICENSE . Impeccable started from Anthropic's frontend-design skill. Created by Paul Bakaus

items.title: agentgateway/agentgateway
items.description: Next Generation Agentic Proxy for AI Agents and MCP servers https://agentgateway.dev first complete connectivity solution for Agentic AI. Agentgateway is an open source proxy built on AI-native protocols (MCP & A2A) that provides drop-in security, observability, and governance for agent-to-LLM, agent-to-tool, and agent-to-agent communication across any framework and environment. Intro to Agentgateway Video Key Features LLM Gateway Route traffic to major LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, and more) through a unified OpenAI-compatible API with budget and spend controls, prompt enrichment, load balancing, and failover. MCP Gateway Connect LLMs to tools and external data sources via MCP with tool federation, stdio/HTTP/SSE/Streamable HTTP transports, OpenAPI integration, and OAuth authentication. A2A Gateway Enable secure agent-to-agent communication using A2A, with capability discovery, modality negotiation, and task collaboration. Inference Routing Intelligent routing to self-hosted models using Kubernetes Inference Gateway extensions, with decisions based on GPU utilization, KV cache, LoRA adapters, and queue depth. Guardrails Multi-layered content filtering with regex, OpenAI moderation, AWS Bedrock Guardrails, Google Model Armor, and custom webhooks. Security & Observability Auth (JWT, API keys, OAuth), fine-grained RBAC with CEL policy engine, rate limiting, TLS, and OpenTelemetry metrics/logs/tracing. Getting Started Standalone Quickstart — Get started with agentgateway in minutes. Kubernetes Quickstart — Deploy on Kubernetes using the built-in controller and Gateway API. Documentation Depending on your deployment environment, check out the following docs: agentgateway.dev/docs: For deployments without the full Kubernetes controller, driven by flat yaml config. agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/latest: For Kubernetes-based deployments using the built-in Kubernetes controller and Gateway API support. Agentgateway has a built-in UI for you to explore agentgateway connecting agent-to-agent or agent-to-tool: Sponsors Thank you to our sponsors for helping to fund the development of agentgateway! Contributing For instructions on how to contribute to the agentgateway project, see the CONTRIBUTION.md file. Community Meetings To join a community meeting, add the agentgateway calendar to your Google account. Then, you can find event details on the calendar. Recordings of the community meetings will be published on our google drive. Roadmap agentgateway is currently in active development. If you'd like a feature that's missing, open an issue in our GitHub repo. Contributors Thanks to all contributors who are helping to make agentgateway better. Agentgateway is a Linux Foundation project.

items.title: akitaonrails/ai-memory
items.description: Solution for long term memory for agent coding CLIs and to facilitate handoff between different agent vendors Long-term memory for AI coding agents. Quit Claude Code mid-task, start OpenAI Codex in the same directory, continue without re-explaining the architecture, the failed approaches, or the open questions. Website: aimemory.sh Why ai-memory Your coding agent probably has a memory feature already. Claude Code takes its own notes, Cursor remembers some things, and every platform is adding more. They all have the same limits: the notes live on one machine, belong to one agent, and drop out of view when you switch tools or hand the work to a teammate. ai-memory removes those limits. It follows you across agents. More than twenty harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Grok, Devin, Kimi, Kiro, and others) feed one shared memory. Quit Claude Code mid-task, open Codex in the same directory, and the next agent picks up a handoff that says where you left off, what failed, and what is still open. Handoffs are a typed protocol: each one has an owner and is claimed exactly once. It can carry the session, not just a summary. Start agents with ai-memory run: quit Claude Code, run ai-memory run codex, and Codex gets the shared workstream plus a private, temporary local projection of Claude's visible native history for exact details the bounded startup packet omitted. The remote server receives only the harness and session identity, never the local transcript path or body. Direct harness launches behave exactly as before. It follows you across projects. A small profile of how you usually work (your package manager, test layout, architecture habits) reaches every new repository at session start, so you stop re-explaining yourself. It sits below each repository's rules file as a default. It is on by default for a single user, and on a shared server it is opt-in and private per person. See docs/cross-project-profile.md. It follows you across machines. Memory lives in a server you run, on the same laptop, a homelab box, or anywhere else, so the project you left on the desktop is the project you resume on the laptop, with the same knowledge and the same open questions. It works for a team. Point everyone at one server, and what one person's sessions learn, everyone's agents can retrieve. Knowledge is shared per project; personal handoffs stay personal. Multi-user auth, per-person attribution, and an audit log are built in and are not a paid tier. Your memory is plain markdown. The source of truth is a git-backed wiki of ordinary .md files: grep it, open it in Obsidian, edit it by hand, rsync it. The database is a derived index that can always be rebuilt from the files. There is no vector store to maintain and no content locked in a binary blob. It captures the work itself, silently. Lifecycle hooks record what happened (prompts, tool calls, session boundaries), sanitize it at a typed privacy boundary before anything is stored, and the server consolidates it into readable pages. You do not have to ask it to remember anything. The default path uses zero LLM calls: capture, search, and handoffs all work with no API key. It ages memory without an LLM. Memory decays on a schedule you can tune per tier, and memory you use decays slower: opening a page, searching it, or reaching it through a link counts as use. When episodic notes go cold they can be compacted down to their durable facts (file paths, error codes, decisions) instead of dropped. Near-duplicates collapse into one, and likely contradictions get flagged, all with zero API calls. Nothing is hard-deleted: the original stays in git and the version chain (restore-page brings it back). Access-weighted retention is always on because it can only keep memory longer. The parts that rewrite or drop content (compaction, dedup, per-tier curves) stay off by default until you turn them on. It can also "dream", if you let it. With an LLM configured, an opt-in background pass rewrites whole clusters of cold notes into single coherent pages while you are idle, and cancels as soon as you come back to work. It never deletes a source (the pre-merge versions stay reachable), it is off by default, and it has to pass a recall eval before it could become default behavior. Unless you ask for more, the zero-LLM path above is what runs. It is honest about itself. It ships as one self-contained binary. Purge commands say exactly what "deleted" means. The write ceiling (~700/s) is measured, not guessed. An audit log records every mutation. How it works capture ──▶ consolidate ──▶ recall ──▶ handoff hooks session-end search next agent, observe summaries as + brief any harness silently wiki pages injection Agents emit sanitized observations through lifecycle hooks as you work. At session end, observations become coherent markdown pages in the project's wiki (optionally LLM-written; useful even without). The next session, in any agent on any machine, gets a bounded brief and can search everything: full-text, entities, links, and (optionally) vectors, fused into one ranking. Cross-agent handoffs pass the baton explicitly. The full design, including the invariants that keep multi-user and multi-session use safe, is in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. An optional server-rendered management console provides user administration, session inspection and deletion, and personal MCP API keys. Build with --features management-ui and start serve --transport http --enable-management-ui; both compile-time and runtime opt-ins are required. Support matrix Every row below is a first-party integration (MCP registration, lifecycle hooks, or both) checked by CI. The full matrix with per-agent notes and caveats is in docs/support-matrix.md. Area Status Linux Supported NixOS module Supported macOS Supported Windows via WSL2 Supported Native Windows Experimental Claude Code Supported Codex Supported Command Code Supported Devin CLI Supported OpenCode (V1/V2 auto-detected; legacy force-V2 aliases retained) Supported Cursor Supported Gemini CLI Supported Oh My Pi / OMP Supported Pi Supported Crush Managed-only Managed workstreams Opt-in Claude Desktop MCP-only OpenClaw Supported Antigravity CLI Supported Grok Build CLI Supported Swival CLI MCP-only Zero Supported ZCode Supported Kimi Code Supported Kiro CLI Supported Pool Hooks-only GitHub Copilot CLI Supported Factory Droid Supported Meta Muse Code Supported CodeBuddy Code Hooks-only IBM Bob Supported Qwen Code Supported Qoder Supported VS Code Copilot MCP-only Zed MCP-only DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Hooks + MCP Cline CLI Hooks + MCP FreeBuff MCP-only Prime Agent MCP-only Hermes Agent Supported GrizzyBot Supported LLM/auth providers Supported Embedding providers Supported Coming from another tool? Most agent-memory tools optimize for one thing: extracting atomic facts per turn, a temporal knowledge graph, an agent-editable memory OS, or a hosted context API. ai-memory is built around a git-backed markdown wiki as the source of truth, with a derived index for retrieval. It captures automatically from lifecycle hooks, is shared across agents, machines, and people, and works with zero LLM calls by default. This table shows what carries over from each tool and what you gain: Coming from… What's similar What you gain Mem0 / fact extractors (LangMem) Automatic per-turn capture Memory compiles into readable pages you own and edit, not opaque fact rows; retrieval fuses FTS + entity + graph (+ local vectors) with no cloud API key Zep / Graphiti (temporal KG) Temporal reasoning, typed relations Bi-temporal-lite (as_of, version-filtered search) and typed edges without standing up a graph database, in one binary mcp-memory-service (fact rows, SQLite) SQLite + local embeddings, hook capture, typed edges, honest numbers, and, on 2.4, per-tier decay curves, extractive compression, DBSCAN cold-cluster dedup, access reinforcement, and contradiction flagging Human-editable markdown pages instead of fact-rows, cross-agent claim-once handoffs, and the same aging machinery done zero-LLM by default, reversibly (supersede-not-delete + restore-page), and off by default basic-memory (file-first markdown) Markdown-on-disk as the source of truth Automatic lifecycle capture and a derived FTS/entity/graph index on top, cross-agent handoffs, and multi-user sharing built in Claude Code built-in memory "Remember my project" convenience, zero setup Synced across machines and agents, searchable, team-capable, and captures tool lifecycle, unlike a per-laptop MEMORY.md Hindsight / OpenViking (LLM or VLM in the loop) Living pages / document memory with a background consolidation loop, plus, on 2.4, belief-strength confidence plus an opt-in LLM "dream" rewrite of cold clusters A self-contained binary that runs zero-LLM by default and keeps memory in markdown files that are the source of truth, not a mirror; claim-once handoffs; the dream/belief features are opt-in, off by default, and never delete a source (vs a mandatory LLM loop) Supermemory / LiquidLM (hosted memory API) A managed second brain with automatic ingestion Git-versioned markdown you own, no required API spend, offline operation, and per-project team sharing; ai-memory remembers this repo, not a general vault Across all of these, ai-memory gives you files you own (git-backed markdown), a zero-LLM default, one self-contained binary, sharing across agents, machines, and teams, automatic lifecycle capture, and typed, claim-once handoffs. Opt-in features (LLM consolidation, vector search, the "dream" consolidation pass, belief-strength in ranking) stay opt-in, and the zero-LLM aging path (per-tier decay, extractive compaction, dedup, contradiction flagging, access-weighted retention) works with no API key at all. Built on the shoulders of: the Karpathy LLM Wiki (compile-not-retrieve), agentmemory (hook capture for coding agents), basic-memory (markdown-on-disk truth), cognee (pipeline composition and triplet embeddings), Hermes Agent (the self-improvement loop), and A-MEM (Zettelkasten-style atomic notes). The full comparison, covering where each approach wins, where ai-memory differs, and the published benchmark, is in How ai-memory compares. Quick start Linux and macOS (two commands, no root) curl -fsSL https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ai-memory setup install.sh downloads the release for your OS and CPU, checks it against the release's published SHA-256 checksum (it refuses to install without a match), and links ~/.local/bin/ai-memory. ai-memory setup then creates the data directory with a bearer token in an owner-only file, starts a per-user service (systemd --user or a launchd LaunchAgent), and wires MCP, hooks and Agent Skills for every agent it finds, or the ones you name with --agent. It shows the plan, with where it found each agent, and asks first: answer y, or type the numbers of the agents to wire. --plan prints the plan and changes nothing, --web shows the plan as a page in your browser and applies the agents you tick there, --yes skips the question, and running it again changes nothing. Afterwards, restart your agents and ask one of them "What do you remember about this project?" to see it answer through ai-memory. Details, the environment variables and how to verify the script before running it are in docs/install.md. An AI agent installing ai-memory for you can follow INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md. Claude Code and Codex users can wire their agent as a marketplace plugin instead (the binary is still installed as above): claude plugin marketplace add akitaonrails/ai-memory && claude plugin install ai-memory@ai-memory codex plugin marketplace add akitaonrails/ai-memory && codex plugin add ai-memory@ai-memory Codex then asks you to trust the hooks in /hooks. See Marketplace plugins. Windows (two commands, no admin) In PowerShell: irm https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex ai-memory setup install.ps1 checks the release zip against its published SHA-256 checksum, unpacks it under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ai-memory and adds that directory to your user PATH. ai-memory setup then does what it does on Linux and macOS, with a logon entry in place of the service: the server starts when you sign in, with no console window, and restarts if it fails. Details and the other Windows setups (WSL2, Docker Desktop, a real Windows service) are in docs/windows.md. Arch Linux (AUR) For native Arch installs, use the AUR packages. They install /usr/bin/ai-memory, packaged hook sources, and both system-level and user-level systemd units. yay -S ai-memory-bin # prebuilt Linux x86_64/aarch64 binary yay -S ai-memory # builds from source ai-memory setup # data dir, user service, agents, self-check Fedora (RPM) Download the x86_64 or aarch64 RPM from the latest release, then install it: sudo dnf install ./ai-memory-*.rpm On a single-user workstation, ai-memory setup then does the rest, as on the two-command path above: data dir and token, a user service, the agents it finds, and a self-check. ai-memory setup System service installs use /var/lib/ai-memory and /etc/ai-memory/ via the packaged unit. Full user-service, system-service, auth, and provider setup is in docs/install.md#arch-linux-native-packages-aur. macOS (menu bar app) A self-contained .app that bundles the native ai-memory binary and hooks/ tree, starts the existing LaunchAgent, and opens /web, ai-memory status, and config.toml from the menu bar. Wiki, SQLite, config, and models stay in ~/Library/Application Support/ai-memory, so replacing the app is an update and does not rewrite that tree. Needs a Rust toolchain and Xcode / Swift 6 (same as a source build): git clone https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory cd ai-memory ./companions/ai-memory-macos/build.sh open "companions/ai-memory-macos/dist/AI Memory.app" Drag AI Memory.app to /Applications, then Install & Start Server from the menu extra (no Dock icon). The app reads the bearer token init wrote into its data dir, so the status item turns green on its own. Then wire your agents with the bundled binary; --no-service leaves the app's LaunchAgent in charge: BIN="/Applications/AI Memory.app/Contents/Resources/runtime/ai-memory" "$BIN" setup --no-service Prebuilt tarball and launchd-without-the-app paths: docs/macos.md. Companion details: companions/ai-memory-macos. Docker You need: Docker or Podman + an agent CLI from the Support Matrix, or anything else that speaks MCP. The published Docker image includes linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 variants, so Apple Silicon Macs and ARM64 Linux hosts can pull akitaonrails/ai-memory without --platform linux/amd64 emulation. The Docker quick-start below has no authentication: the container never runs init, so it starts without a token. The server binds to loopback only, so nothing outside the machine can reach it, but local processes and browser pages can. Native installs that run ai-memory init get a bearer token by default; see Security below for that and for adding a token here. # 1. Install the ai-memory CLI wrapper (a small shell script that # runs the binary inside a container with your $HOME mounted). This is # the only thing that needs to live on the host filesystem. mkdir -p ~/.local/bin wrapper_tmp="$(mktemp -d)" trap 'rm -rf "$wrapper_tmp"' EXIT wrapper_base=https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/releases/latest/download/ai-memory-wrapper curl -fsSL "$wrapper_base" -o "$wrapper_tmp/ai-memory-wrapper" curl -fsSL "$wrapper_base.sha256" -o "$wrapper_tmp/ai-memory-wrapper.sha256" expected="$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }' "$wrapper_tmp/ai-memory-wrapper.sha256")" if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then actual="$(sha256sum "$wrapper_tmp/ai-memory-wrapper" | awk '{ print $1 }')" else actual="$(shasum -a 256 "$wrapper_tmp/ai-memory-wrapper" | awk '{ print $1 }')" fi [ -n "$expected" ] && [ "$actual" = "$expected" ] || { echo "wrapper checksum mismatch" >&2; exit 1; } install -m 0755 "$wrapper_tmp/ai-memory-wrapper" ~/.local/bin/ai-memory rm -rf "$wrapper_tmp" trap - EXIT # Most distros put ~/.local/bin on PATH automatically. If `which # ai-memory` comes up empty, add this to ~/.bashrc / ~/.zshrc: # export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" # 2. Start the server. `--restart unless-stopped` makes it come back # on docker daemon restart and on machine boot (provided your # docker service is enabled at boot — `sudo systemctl enable # docker` on most distros). Loopback-only bind (`127.0.0.1:49374`) # so nothing outside this machine can reach it. Omit the LLM / # EMBEDDING lines for zero-LLM mode — FTS5 search still works # without any keys. docker run -d --name ai-memory \ --restart unless-stopped \ -p 127.0.0.1:49374:49374 \ -v ai-memory-data:/data \ -e AI_MEMORY_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic \ -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... \ -e AI_MEMORY_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai \ -e OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... \ docker.io/akitaonrails/ai-memory:latest # 3. Wire your agent CLI in two commands. The wrapper takes care of # mounts and each client's config-path detection. Re-run with # `--agent codex`, `--agent command-code`, `--agent devin`, `--agent opencode`, `--agent opencode2`, `--agent gemini-cli`, # `--agent grok`, `--agent kimi-code`, `--agent kiro-cli`, `--agent copilot-cli`, `--agent droid`, `--agent muse`, `--agent cline`, `--agent qwen-code`, `--agent qoder`, `--agent omp`, # `--agent oh-my-pi`, `--client cursor`, # `--client gemini-cli`, `--client grok`, `--client kiro-cli`, # `--client cline`, `--client freebuff`, etc. # for additional agents; full list in docs/install.md. ai-memory install-mcp --client claude-code --apply ai-memory install-hooks --agent claude-code --apply On Linux and macOS, the Docker wrapper runs install-hooks through its checksum-verified native host client. Global options may precede the command, for example ai-memory --config /path/to/config.toml run codex; the native client receives the complete argument list. The installed hooks therefore enforce client-side capture controls such as [capture] ignore_paths and allowlist mode before an event reaches the spool or network. Set AI_MEMORY_HOOK_PLATFORM=posix explicitly only when you need the legacy shell compatibility path; the installer warns that path cannot enforce capture policy v1. The examples use docker; replace it with podman on a Podman host. The wrapper automatically uses Podman when Docker is not installed. Set AI_MEMORY_DOCKER=podman to force Podman when both engines are available. That completes the setup on Linux/macOS. Start a Claude Code session as usual: every prompt and tool call now lands in ai-memory, and the next session you open in this project will see a handoff with where you left off. On macOS the native binary is the recommended path when you do not need Docker, either through the menu bar app above or a release tarball / launchd agent. Later updates for that path use ai-memory upgrade (checksum-verified GitHub release replace + hook refresh); see docs/install.md#keeping-ai-memory-up-to-date. The same native upgrade path covers Windows x86_64 zip installs under a writable prefix (see docs/windows.md Scenario C). Upgrading a 2.x install of any kind to 3.0? Read docs/upgrading-to-3.0.md first. Wiring another agent is the same two commands with a different name: --client codex, --agent codex, and so on for every row of the support matrix. OpenCode is version-detected by host-side commands; when generating its artifacts inside a container, use setup-agent --agent opencode --opencode-dialect v1|v2 --to /tmp/unused because the container cannot inspect the host executable. The legacy opencode2, opencode-v2, and open-code2 aliases remain force-V2 compatibility spellings for old scripts; use opencode for new commands. The full per-agent guide, including Windows and remote servers, is docs/install.md. Two agents in the same project at once, or teammates on one server, work out of the box: the "current project" pointer is isolated per caller by default (v1.39+). See docs/auto-scope.md for the optional session-aware Claude Code bridge and the details. If in doubt, start your harness with ai-memory run. It is the preferred way to launch: the first time it runs a harness it auto-installs that harness's ai-memory hooks + MCP if they are missing (so capture and recall work without a separate install-hooks/install-mcp step to forget), it wires the right project scope by construction, and it adds cross-harness session continuity on top of shared memory. Everything is idempotent and one-time per harness and config home. If the server is unreachable, run warns and launches anyway with local capture spooling; run ai-memory recover after the server returns (see Degraded offline launches). Pass --require-server to fail closed instead. ai-memory run claude ai-memory run codex --yolo # same workstream + local Claude history dossier ai-memory run --profile work claude # reusable config.toml env/account preset ai-memory continue # resume the newest managed checkout # after a dead launcher left its lease behind (same operator only) ai-memory run --force-unlock codex ai-memory resume # pick from ALL workstreams in this checkout only ai-memory resume --search auth # find a workstream by name (case-insensitive) ai-memory resume --all # pick across every linked checkout --force-unlock immediately expires the selected workstream's active lease; use it only when you know the previous launcher is gone. It does not kill a native process, and it cannot evict another authenticated operator's run. See the managed-workstream recovery notes for the full safety contract. On a real harness switch, the receiving managed agent is told to consult AI_MEMORY_PREVIOUS_SESSION_HISTORY when you ask to continue and the bounded portable packet lacks a detail. The variable names a private temporary Markdown projection created from the previous harness's checkout-validated, read-only adapter; the file disappears when the managed child exits. It is local to the launcher machine. This covers quota exhaustion and other abrupt exits where the old harness cannot write a handoff: refreshed ai-memory routing also tells the new agent that "continue", "resume", and "pick up where we left off" mean to read that file first when the three managed-run variables are present. A switch on another machine still gets the server's portable ledger and handoff, but cannot read a native transcript that exists only on the first machine. Without the managed launcher, a harness cut off the same way leaves no handoff at all, so the next one could pick up an older handoff or session page. When the newest captured work in the project is in another of your sessions that never ended and left no handoff after that work, the next session start carries a one-line notice that names that session. The agent then reads its newest prompts and tool results with memory_read_session_observations. The same session is listed first in memory_briefing's recent_sessions, and memory_handoff_list names it as newer_unended_session. If that variable is absent on a real same-machine switch, run type -a ai-memory and ai-memory --version in the launching shell. This path requires the 3.1.0 or newer host client; a stale Cargo or package-manager binary earlier in PATH can shadow an updated wrapper. In resume, type to search, use Up/Down to select a workstream, and Left/Right to choose its harness. Enter launches the selection; Escape clears a search, then cancels when the search is empty (Ctrl-C always cancels). The list scrolls and loads every checkout-local page; there is no default workstream cutoff. Use --limit N only when you want to cap the matching results. Workstreams from other repositories or worktrees are left out unless you pass --all, which lists every linked checkout (the current one first); continue still resumes the newest linked checkout from anywhere. Listing reads Git identity only; it does not scan the working tree with git status before showing the picker. Full checkpoints are still captured when launching the selected workstream. Auto-wiring is on by default; opt out with ai-memory run --no-autowire or AI_MEMORY_RUN_AUTOWIRE=false. You can still wire agents by hand with install-hooks / install-mcp (e.g. for a harness you never launch through ai-memory run). ai-memory uninstall --apply removes everything ai-memory installed, and only what it installed. It also clears ai-memory run's auto-wire record, so the next managed launch wires that harness again; to keep it unwired, launch with --no-autowire or set AI_MEMORY_RUN_AUTOWIRE=false. Install commands are idempotent and write timestamped backups next to any file they touch. NixOS This flake ships a NixOS module (nixosModules.default) with a systemd.services.ai-memory unit: a dedicated ai-memory system user (nologin, no linger) plus a hardened systemd sandbox (ProtectSystem = "strict", empty capability sets, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, RestrictAddressFamilies, and the rest; see nix/systemd-sandbox.nix). Packaged FHS units under packaging/systemd/ keep their existing lighter hardening. The flake exports packages for x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux, and aarch64-darwin. Intel macOS remains supported by the release tarball and Homebrew, but not by the pinned Nixpkgs revision. { inputs.ai-memory.url = "github:akitaonrails/ai-memory"; outputs = { nixpkgs, ai-memory, ... }: { nixosConfigurations.myhost = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem { system = "x86_64-linux"; modules = [ ai-memory.nixosModules.default { services.ai-memory = { enable = true; # enableWeb = true; # off by default — the web UI is opt-in # enableApi = true; # API-only companions; no browser UI settings = { allowed_hosts = [ "localhost" "127.0.0.1" "::1" "homelab.example" ]; log_level = "info"; }; # Loopback (default): secrets optional; missing env file is tolerated. # Non-loopback: set one of ageSecret, sopsSecret, or environmentFile. # ageSecret = "ai-memory-env"; # config.age.secrets. (agenix) # sopsSecret = "ai-memory/env"; # config.sops.secrets. (sops-nix) }; } ]; }; }; } Declarative non-secret config lives in services.ai-memory.settings (a small typed set for common keys, plus freeformType for the rest of config.toml). The module renders a generated TOML file and passes --config. Top-level bind, port, and enableWeb win over duplicate settings keys. Anything in settings (including llm_headers) lands in a world-readable Nix store path, so do not put API keys there. Secrets such as AI_MEMORY_AUTH_TOKEN never go in settings or the world-readable Nix store. This includes llm_headers, which can carry API credentials; set AI_MEMORY_LLM_HEADERS in ageSecret, sopsSecret, or environmentFile instead. These three secret sources are mutually exclusive. Non-loopback binds require one; loopback may omit them and tolerates a missing environment file (systemd EnvironmentFile=-…). Put TLS in front of a LAN/WAN bind; see docs/https-via-proxy.md. All options and defaults are in nix/nixos-module.nix. The module is entirely opt-in: nix build, nix run, nix develop, and the CLI are unchanged if you don't import it. git is a runtime dependency. Hook capture and ai-memory doctor run it to read the repository a session works in. The module puts pkgs.git on the service's PATH. The package itself leaves the binary unwrapped, because a wrapper renames the running process and the live-process guard in reset, restore, reindex and uninstall --purge-data looks for a process named ai-memory. If you install the package without the module (nix profile install, home.packages), install git next to it. Everyday use Day to day, you mostly do not think about ai-memory. Hooks capture prompts, tool calls, and session boundaries; session end turns them into readable wiki pages; the next session starts with a handoff. Ask "where did we leave off?" to continue from the pending handoff. Import a local PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, Markdown file, or VTT/SRT transcript as attributed, sanitized memory with the optional ai-memory-importer document command. Ask "have we discussed X?" or "search memory for Y" to query the wiki. Narrow a large wiki before ranking with memory_query filters such as path_prefix: "procedures/", tag: "rust", kind: "decision", or tier: "procedural". Inspect content-free per-workload LLM call, outcome, latency, and usage telemetry with ai-memory status --json; it diagnoses the configured provider but does not route different workloads to different models. Ask "catch me up" for a prose digest of recent project activity, or run ai-memory recent (--global for every project) to list the newest pages. Search Chinese, Japanese and Korean text without spaces: zero-LLM search matches unspaced Han, Kana and Hangul substrings. Run ai-memory bootstrap once when adopting an existing project with months of history. Start the server with --enable-web for a read-only browser view of the wiki, a link graph at /web/graph, a root/operator managed-workstream overview at /web/workstreams, and a JSON API under /api/v1. On a server with a bearer token and no user accounts (every fresh install), the browser asks for a username and password: any username, and the contents of /auth-tokens/default as the password. Investigate Claude Code and Codex response-token usage in the project dashboard, and pick a Light, Dark or System theme. See Investigate token usage for capture coverage, cache accounting and the investigation flags. You can drill down from a project to an agent, its sessions and individual responses. The web agent inbox lets an operator queue requests for registered agents and read the received and sent history. Token filters run on the full authorized ledger, with native turn and tool context when reported. Pages show their sources, declared contradictions and recall explanations, and the feature guide shows the effective installation states in the web UI. Back up host-side harness configuration with ai-memory backup-agents -o agent-assets.tar.gz; inspect a restore with ai-memory restore-agents -i agent-assets.tar.gz, then add --apply only after reviewing the active skills, plugins, instructions, and destinations. Search modes, entities, feedback, briefings, and the web API are covered in docs/usage.md and docs/use-cases.md. Teams and multiple machines Run the server somewhere reachable, such as a homelab box or a LAN host, and point every machine and every teammate at it. Knowledge is shared per project; personal handoffs stay personal; every write is attributed and audited. Multi-user auth (passwords, API credentials) is built in. Start with docs/users.md for accounts and ownership, and docs/deploy.md for the server itself. It includes measured capacity numbers and the one rule you must follow: one server per data directory, never two. Two opt-in HTTP surfaces build on the same browser sign-in, and both are off by default. serve --enable-session-management lets signed-in users inspect sessions and purge the ones they own (docs/session-management.md). serve --enable-self-service-keys lets them issue and revoke their own aim_ API keys (docs/self-service-keys.md). Security The server binds to loopback only by default. A fresh ai-memory init also mints a root bearer token into the data dir, which the hooks, the CLI and the ai-memory mcp-bridge stdio bridge read from there; it is never written into a harness config. An install created before that default (and the Docker quick-start) runs without auth until ai-memory auth enable, and ai-memory status says so. From there, hardening is incremental: a bearer token for the LAN, per-user accounts, OIDC device auth for hooks, TLS via a reverse proxy. Capture is sanitized at a typed privacy boundary before anything is stored, and per-repository [capture] rules can exclude paths or invert to allowlist mode. A repository can also route its capture to a different server than the one the hooks were installed against. Human login beyond loopback requires an HTTPS posture by default. Operators who explicitly accept plaintext passwords, cookies, credentials, and memory traffic on a private LAN can opt in with serve --allow-insecure-human-auth; the server never enables that exception implicitly. The full model is in docs/security.md, docs/users.md, and docs/https-via-proxy.md. For data-flow, identity/SSO, and offline-install questions specifically, see DATA_HANDLING.md, docs/sso.md, and docs/airgapped-install.md. LLM providers Optional. Everything works with zero LLM calls; adding a provider upgrades session summaries and enables semantic search. Anthropic, OpenAI (including OAuth), Codex CLI credential reuse, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, OpenCode (Go and Zen), the Cursor Agent CLI (cursor), and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) are supported for consolidation; OpenAI, Voyage, Gemini, and keyless OpenAI-compatible endpoints for embeddings. Configuration lives in docs/llm-providers.md. For optional synthesized query answers, operators can set [query_answer] max_context_tokens to limit admitted evidence while retaining all retrieval hits. Known newer corrections take priority, and whole snippets are preferred over sentence-bounded fragments. It is disabled by default. See the configuration reference for the conservative counting rule and omission receipt. Architecture One Rust binary runs an MCP/HTTP server and owns one data directory: / ├── wiki/ # markdown source of truth, git-versioned ├── raw/ # immutable sanitized managed-workstream transcript segments ├── db/ # SQLite indexes, including FTS5, entities, and embeddings ├── models/ # reserved for local embedding models └── logs/ # rolling tracing output Hooks POST observations to the server. The server serializes writes through one SQLite writer, compiles session observations into markdown pages, and serves retrieval through FTS5, entity-match and graph-neighbor RRF, optional vector RRF, an observation-evidence stream that lifts a session's page when its captured turns match (on by default), bounded source-authority adjustment, and bounded raw-observation fallback for non-global searches. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for the data-flow diagram, crate breakdown, schema notes, and invariants. Docs For users File What it is docs/testing-dashboard.md Dashboard behavior tests, real-browser CI and mutation probes that prove regression guards fail. docs/cookbook.md Task-oriented cheat sheet. "I want to do X" → how: recall prior work, keep a project rule, import an existing knowledge base, get two agents/repos working together. Start here. docs/install.md Installation cookbook. Every agent CLI, every alternative (curl, source build, no-docker, no-auth), and the server-on-a-different-machine walkthrough. docs/usage.md Handoffs, proactive memory queries, slim routing snippet + managed Agent Skills, web UI, raw-wiki inspection, and the rules, memory and profile precedence. docs/cross-project-profile.md The cross-project profile. Your usual choices delivered to every project as defaults: defaults per deployment, every setting, per-project opt-outs, multi-user opt-in and privacy, CLI. docs/managed-workstreams.md Optional ai-memory run continuity across harnesses: auto harness selection, native resume, argument forwarding, ledger search, privacy, and recovery. docs/agent-messaging.md Cross-project agent-to-agent messaging: a directed, claim-once inbox/queue plus the on-start "you have mail" notice. docs/marker-file.md Default repository-path project naming plus .ai-memory.toml workspace/project routing for multi-client trees, mono-repos, worktrees, and work/personal separation, plus per-repository server profiles. docs/auto-scope.md [auto_scope] modes for shared servers: the default per_actor isolation, session-aware per_session isolation, and the pre-v1.39 single slot. docs/macos.md macOS install paths: menu bar app, native release tarball, source build, Docker wrapper, launchd, and current limitations. docs/windows.md Windows install modes: full WSL2, native Windows with Docker Desktop, prebuilt native release zip, native source builds, and caveats. docs/mcp-install.md Per-client MCP and lifecycle notes, handoff-injection limits, and community bridge guidance. docs/programmatic-memory.md Use ai-memory from any tool: MCP write/query/handoff calls, scope rules and incremental reads. docs/deploy.md Homelab deploy: bin/deploy, bearer-token auth, pointers to the TLS guide. docs/users.md Multi-user attribution and human login. Four-rung bearer ladder, password sessions, ai-memory user / api-key walkthrough, brownfield migration. docs/management-ui.md Optional server-rendered console: feature gates, user and session management, MCP keys, public deployment, and frontend checks. docs/https-via-proxy.md HTTPS via a reverse proxy. When you need TLS and when you don't, with copy-paste Caddy / nginx / Cloudflare Tunnel templates and the "secure when you're not" failure modes. docs/lifecycle-ops.md Read before purge / rename / merge / backup / restore / reset / reindex / restore-page. Safety matrix, lossless project-identity merge, per-project disk layout, retained-version recovery, and operator workflows. docs/backup.md Backing up the wiki + data dir to a remote git repository: what to include, what to exclude, scheduled push pattern, restore, and security posture. Companion to docs/lifecycle-ops.md (which covers the on-box ai-memory backup snapshot). docs/design-backup-agent-assets.md Host agent-asset backup/restore: supported paths, filtering, redaction limits, archive bounds, active-content warning, and rollback behavior. docs/llm-providers.md Provider configuration for consolidation and embeddings. docs/security.md The full security model. docs/support-matrix.md The full agent/platform matrix with notes. docs/use-cases.md Scenario walkthroughs. DATA_HANDLING.md Data-flow reference for security/legal review. What's stored, what's local-only, the two opt-in external paths, and how deletion/retention work. docs/sso.md Enterprise identity: the OIDC device-auth flow, its scope, and how to front the server with an OIDC-aware gateway. docs/airgapped-install.md Offline/air-gapped install: self-contained build, checksum-verified release binaries, and offline local embedding models. docs/upgrading-to-3.0.md Upgrading a 2.x install to 3.0: what changed, the removed token commands and their replacements, upgrade steps, and rollback. docs/MIGRATION-2.0.md Upgrading an existing store to 2.0: the backup-gated automatic migration and how to restore. docs/benchmarks/ Published retrieval-quality numbers with provenance, reproducible from the in-repo harness. docs/okf.md The wiki is natively an Open Knowledge Format (OKF v0.2) bundle; design and field mapping.
